akhfash:4-4.t: He said ﴿بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾, that is: (able) to gather (أَنْ نَجْمعَ); that is: "yes, We gather them, being able" (بَلَى نَجْمَعُها قادِرِين). The singular of "البَنَان" (fingertips) is بَنَانَة.

akhfash:10-10.t:
And He said ﴿أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ﴾, that is: where is the fleeing (الفِرار)? The poet said [in the madīd metre; this is the two hundred and seventy-third verse cited as evidence]:
يا لَبَكْرِ أنْشرُوا لِي كُلَيْبَاً * يا لَبَكْرِ أَيْنَ أَيْنَ الفِرار
(O clan of Bakr, bring Kulayb back to life for me! O clan of Bakr, where, where is the flight?)
Because every maṣdar (verbal noun) built on this pattern is made "مَفْعَل"; and when He means the place, He says ﴿المَفِرّ﴾. It has also been read ﴿أَيْنَ المَفِرّ﴾, because everything whose verb is on the pattern "يَفْعِل" has its "مَفْعِل" with kasra, such as "المَضْرِب" when you mean the place in which one strikes.

akhfash:14-14.t: And He said ﴿بَلِ ٱلإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾: He made him himself the evidence (البصيرة), as you say to a man "أَنْتَ حُجَّةٌ على نَفْسِكَ" ("you are a proof against yourself").

akhfash:22-23.t: [And] He said ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ﴾, that is: beautiful; ﴿إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾: by looking to Allah He means — and Allah knows best — (looking) to what comes to them of His blessings and provision. And you may say "وَاللهِ ما أَنْظُرُ إِلاَّ إِلَى اللهِ وإِلَيْكَ" ("by Allah, I look only to Allah and to you"), that is: I await what is with Allah and what is with you.

akhfash:31-31.t: And He said ﴿فَلاَ صَدَّقَ وَلاَ صَلَّىٰ﴾, that is: he did not believe and did not pray (فَلَمْ يصدّق ولم يصلّ), as you say "ذَهَبَ فَلاَ جاءَني ولا جاءَك" ("he went away, and came neither to me nor to you").

akhfash:40-40.t: And He said ﴿عَلَىٰ أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾; and some read ﴿يُحيِ الموتى﴾, concealing it (ikhfāʾ) and placing it between assimilation (idghām) and non-assimilation. It is not correct for it to be assimilated here, because the final yāʾ does not remain in one state, [since] it becomes an alif in your saying "يَحْيَا" and is dropped in the jussive. So assimilation is not binding on it, and nothing is possible in it except ikhfāʾ (concealment), which is between idghām and clear pronunciation (bayān).

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿لَا﴾ redundant (zāʾida) in both places ﴿أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ﴾ which blames itself even if it has striven hard in doing good. The answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected", indicated by:

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسَانُ﴾ i.e. the unbeliever ﴿أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ﴾ for the resurrection and bringing back to life?

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿بَلَى﴾ We will gather them, ﴿قَادِرِينَ﴾ along with gathering them, ﴿عَلَى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾ which is the fingers, i.e. We restore their bones as they were despite their smallness, so how much more the large ones?

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ﴾ the lām is redundant (zāʾida), and it is in the accusative by an implied أَنْ, i.e. to deny ﴿أَمَامَهُ﴾ i.e. the Day of Resurrection, as indicated by:

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ﴾ when ﴿يَوْمُ الْقِيَمَةِ﴾ a question of mockery and denial.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿فَإِذَا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ﴾ with kasra on the rāʾ and with fatḥa; it is dazed and bewildered at what it sees of what it used to deny,

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ﴾ darkens and its light goes,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ﴾ so they rise from the west, or their light goes; and that is on the Day of Resurrection,

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿يَقُولُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ﴾ the fleeing.

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a deterrent from seeking to flee; ﴿لَا وَزَرَ﴾ no refuge in which to fortify oneself.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ﴾ the resting place of all creatures, and they are reckoned and recompensed.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿يُنَبَّأُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ﴾ of the first of his deeds and the last of them.

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾ a witness: his limbs speak of his deeds; the hāʾ [i.e. tāʾ marbūṭa] is for intensiveness; so his recompense is inevitable,

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَلَوْ أَلْقَى مَعَاذِيرَهُ﴾ plural of مَعْذِرَة, irregularly; i.e. even if he brought every excuse, it would not be accepted from him. Allah the Exalted said to His Prophet:

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ﴾ with the Quran, before Gabriel has finished it, ﴿لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ﴾ for fear that it escapes you.

celaleyn:17-17.t: ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ﴾ in your breast ﴿وَقُرْآنَهُ﴾ your reciting it, i.e. its flowing on your tongue.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ﴾ to you, by Gabriel's recitation, ﴿فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ﴾ listen to his recitation; so he ﷺ would listen and then recite it.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ﴾ by making you understand. The connection between this ayah and what precedes it is that that one involved turning away from Allah's signs, and this one involves hastening to them by memorising them.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an opening particle (istiftāḥ) in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿بَلْ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ﴾ this world; with yāʾ and with tāʾ [تُحِبُّونَ] in both verbs,

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَيَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ and so do not work for it [وَتَذَرُونَ].

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ i.e. on the Day of Resurrection ﴿نَاضِرَةٌ﴾ beautiful and radiant,

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ﴾ i.e. they will see Allah, glorified and exalted is He, in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿تَظُنُّ﴾ are certain ﴿أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾ a great calamity that breaks the vertebrae (faqār) of the back.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ in the sense of أَلَا; ﴿إِذَا بَلَغَتِ﴾ the soul ﴿التَّرَاقِيَ﴾ the bones of the throat,

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ those around him say: ﴿مَنْ رَاقٍ﴾ to recite incantations over him so that he may be cured?

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿وَظَنَّ﴾ the one whose soul has reached that is certain ﴿أَنَّهُ الْفِرَاقُ﴾ parting from this world,

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ﴾ i.e. one of his legs with the other at death; i.e. the hardship of parting from this world is entwined with the hardship of the Hereafter's approach;

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿إِلَى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ﴾ i.e. the driving; this indicates what governs إِذَا; the meaning is: when the soul reaches the throat, it is driven to the judgement of its Lord.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿فَلَا صَدَّقَ﴾ the human being ﴿وَلَا صَلَّى﴾ i.e. he did not believe and did not pray,

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى﴾ strutting in his walk out of self-admiration.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿أَوْلَى لَكَ﴾ there is in it a shift (iltifāt) from the third person; the word is a verbal noun (ism fiʿl), and the lām is for clarification; i.e. may what you hate befall you; ﴿فَأَوْلَى﴾ i.e. for it is more fitting for you than for anyone else.

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ﴾ thinks ﴿الْإِنْسَانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى﴾ neglected, not charged with the laws? I.e. he should not think that.

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ﴾ i.e. he was ﴿نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ تُمْنَى﴾ with tāʾ and with yāʾ [يُمْنَى], poured into the womb,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿ثُمَّ كَانَ﴾ the semen ﴿عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ﴾ Allah from it the human being ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾ proportioned his limbs,

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ﴾ from the semen that became a clinging clot, i.e. a piece of blood, then a chewed lump, i.e. a piece of flesh, ﴿الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ the two kinds, ﴿الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى﴾ they sometimes come together and sometimes each one comes alone without the other.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ﴾ the doer of these things ﴿بِقَادِرٍ عَلَى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتَى﴾ He ﷺ said: "Yes indeed."

daas-irab:1-2.t: ﴿لا أُقْسِمُ﴾ redundant (zāʾida), and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلا أُقْسِمُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿بِالنَّفْسِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿اللَّوَّامَةِ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa).

daas-irab:3-4.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿أن﴾ lightened from the heavy (anna), and its noun is the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and ﴿لن نَجْمَعَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by lan, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عِظامَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the lightened an, and the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب; and ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer; and ﴿قادِرِينَ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; and ﴿أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بَنانَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ʿalā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادرين.

daas-irab:5-6.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); and ﴿يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿لِيَفْجُرَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); and ﴿أَمامَهُ﴾ an adverb of place; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. And ﴿يَسْئَلُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿أَيَّانَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿يَوْمُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾; the nominal clause stands in place of the two objects of يسأل, and the clause «يسأل..» is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-10.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿جُمِعَ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿الشَّمْسُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿الْقَمَرُ﴾ conjoined to الشمس; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿يَقُولُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ يوم is an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿أَيْنَ﴾ an interrogative noun in the position of an accusative (manṣūb) as an adverb of place, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿الْمَفَرُّ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:11-13.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation; and ﴿وَزَرَ﴾ its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), and the khabar (predicate) is omitted; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿الْمُسْتَقَرُّ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿يُنَبَّؤُا﴾ a passive imperfect verb; and ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is resumptive; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to its like; and ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿قَدَّمَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿وَأَخَّرَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قدم.

daas-irab:14-15.t: ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of digression and transition (iḍrāb wa-intiqāl); and ﴿الْإِنْسانُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿عَلى نَفْسِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿بَصِيرَةٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾ the wāw is of ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لَوْ﴾ redundant (zāʾida); and ﴿أَلْقى﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مَعاذِيرَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is a ḥāl.

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿لا تُحَرِّكْ﴾ an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿لِسانَكَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿لِتَعْجَلَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl), and the fāʿil is latent; and ﴿بِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to تحرك. And ﴿إِنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb; and ﴿عَلَيْنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the omitted, fronted khabar (predicate) of inna; and ﴿جَمْعَهُ﴾ its postponed noun; and ﴿قُرْآنَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; the clause is causal (taʿlīl) to the prohibition, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-19.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿قَرَأْناهُ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation; and ﴿فَاتَّبِعْ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿قُرْآنَهُ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. And ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ﴾ parsed like «إن علينا جمعه».

daas-irab:20-21.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); and ﴿تُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿تَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:22-25.t: ﴿وُجُوهٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb annexed to its like; and ﴿ناضِرَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِلى رَبِّها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second khabar. ﴿ناظِرَةٌ﴾ a second khabar. ﴿وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. And ﴿تَظُنُّ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿أَنْ يُفْعَلَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an; and ﴿بِها﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿فاقِرَةٌ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb stands in place of the two objects of تظن, and the verbal clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of وجوه.

daas-irab:26-30.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿إِذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive; and ﴿بَلَغَتِ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿التَّراقِيَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿راقٍ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl), and the clause «قيل..» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَظَنَّ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿أَنَّهُ﴾ anna and its noun; and ﴿الْفِراقُ﴾ its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar stands in place of the two objects of ظن, and the clause «ظن..» is conjoined to what precedes it. And ﴿وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿بِالسَّاقِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. And ﴿إِلى رَبِّكَ﴾ a fronted khabar; and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ an adverb of time annexed to its like; and ﴿الْمَساقُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-35.t: ﴿فَلا﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿صَدَّقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf). ﴿وَلا صَلَّى﴾ conjoined to «فلا صدق». ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a particle of rectification (istidrāk); and ﴿كَذَّبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿وَتَوَلَّى﴾ conjoined to كذب. And ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿ذَهَبَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿إِلى أَهْلِهِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿يَتَمَطَّى﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿أَوْلى﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿لَكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿فَأَوْلى﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿أَوْلى﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى﴾ is conjoined to it.

daas-irab:36-37.t: ﴿أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿أَنْ يُتْرَكَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and its fāʿil is latent (mustatir) [Translator's note: so in the source; for a passive verb this is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent)]; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سُدىً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb stands in place of the two objects of يحسب. And ﴿أَلَمْ يَكُ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, and its noun is latent; and ﴿نُطْفَةً﴾ khabar (predicate); and ﴿مِنْ مَنِيٍّ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of نطفة; and ﴿يُمْنى﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent; the clause is an adjective (naʿt).

daas-irab:38-39.t:
﴿ثُمَّ كانَ﴾ a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿عَلَقَةً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.
And ﴿فَخَلَقَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾ conjoined to فخلق; and ﴿فَجَعَلَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿الزَّوْجَيْنِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿الذَّكَرَ﴾ badal (substitute) of الزوجين; and ﴿الْأُنْثى﴾ conjoined to الذكر.

daas-irab:40-40.t: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the demonstrative is its noun; and ﴿بِقادِرٍ﴾ genitive (majrūr) in form, accusative (manṣūb) in position as the khabar (predicate) of laysa; the clause is resumptive; and ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition; and ﴿أَنْ يُحْيِيَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿الْمَوْتى﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, and both are attached to (mutaʿalliq) قادر.

dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بَنانَهُ): البنان are the fingertips; it is a plural, or a collective noun, of بنانة — two views. In al-Mukhtār: «البنانة is the singular of البنان, which are the fingertips. One says بنان مخضّب (dyed fingertips, in the masculine), because every plural between which and its singular there is nothing but the hāʾ is treated as both feminine and masculine».
(بَرِقَ): برق يبرق, of the class of دخل, برقا, بروقا, برقانا and بريقا: البرق (the lightning) appeared; the thing shone and glittered; the sky: lightning appeared from it; the man: threatened. And برِق يبرَق, of the class of تعب, برقا: he was bewildered and dazed and could not see. It has been read both ways.
(خَسَفَ): it darkened and its light went.
(وَزَرَ): a refuge in which one fortifies oneself; everything you take refuge in, whether a mountain or other, and escape by, is your وزر.

* I'rab:
(لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ): Al-Zamakhsharī said: bringing لا before the verb of oath is widespread in their speech and their poems. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
ولا وأبيك ابنة العامريّ ... لا يدّعي القوم أني أفرّ
(No, by your father, daughter of al-ʿĀmirī, the people shall not claim that I flee.)
The entry of the negative لا before the oath was common in the tongue of the Arabs only because it is usually for rejecting and negating the opponent's claim; so the implied form is: "no, that does not happen, by the right of your father". Ghawiyya ibn Salmā said:
ألا نادت أمامة باحتمال ... لتحزنني فلا بك ما أبالي
(Lo, Umāma called out the departure, to grieve me — no, by you, I do not care.)
Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its benefit is the emphasis of the oath. They said it is a connective (ṣila), like that in «لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب». It was objected that it is added only in the middle of speech, not at its beginning; and they answered that the Qurʾān is like a single sūra, its parts connected with one another. The objection is valid, because it has not occurred as redundant except in the middle of speech, but the answer is not sound — do you not see how Imruʾ al-Qays added it at the opening of his ode? The right view is to say it is for negation, and the meaning is that He does not swear by a thing except to magnify it; His saying, the Exalted, «فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم، وإنه لقسم لو تعلمون عظيم» shows you that. So it is as though, by bringing in the particle of negation, He says:
My magnifying it by swearing by it is as no magnifying, meaning that it deserves more than that. It has also been said that لا negates speech and rejects it before the oath, as though they denied the resurrection, and it was said: No — i.e. the matter is not as you have said — and then it was said: I swear by the Day of Resurrection». It has also been said that it is a rejection of their speech when they denied the resurrection, as though He said: the matter is not as you have said; I swear by the Day of Resurrection. This is the view of al-Farrāʾ and many grammarians. Discussion of it preceded in al-Wāqiʿa, so renew your acquaintance with it. أقسم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), whose fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being أنا; بيوم القيامة is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أقسم.
(وَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ): conjoined to the previous clause; اللوامة is a naʿt (adjective) of النفس, i.e. the one that blames itself on the Day of Resurrection for whatever shortcoming it committed, or the one that never ceases to blame itself in this world. It is narrated that he, upon him be peace, said: «There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but it will blame itself on the Day of Resurrection: if it did good, it will say: Why did I not do more? And if it did evil, it will say: Would that I had refrained from evil». The answer to the oath is omitted, i.e. "you will surely be resurrected", indicated by what follows it, which is:
(أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظامَهُ): the hamza is for a question of denial and rebuke; يحسب is an imperfect verb, nominative; الإنسان is the agent. أن is lightened from the heavy (أنّ); its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and لن and what lies within its scope are in the position of the khabar (predicate); the separator here is the particle of negation. The lightened أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يحسب. عظامه is the object of نجمع, for resurrection and bringing back to life. Al-Naḥḥās said: He singled out the bones only because they are the mould of the body.
(بَلى قادِرِينَ عَلى أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنانَهُ): بلى is a particle of answer; it affirms what comes after the negation over which the question extends. قادرين is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of the implied verb indicated by the particle of answer, i.e. "yes, We will gather them, being able"; this is the right view. Some said it is accusative as the khabar of a concealed كان, i.e. "yes, We were able in the beginning"; and that is not so good. قادرون was read in the nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "yes, We are able". على is a preposition; the maṣdariyya أن and what lies within its scope are interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun) made genitive by على, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to قادرين. The agent of نسوي is a latent pronoun, its implied form being نحن, and بنانه is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). According to Sībawayh, قادرين is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being نجمعها قادرين.
(بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمامَهُ): بل is a conjunction for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī). يريد is conjoined to أيحسب, so it may, like it, be a question, or it may be an affirmation. بل may also be for mere transitional digression without conjunction, as though He turned away from the first speech and took up another. يريد الإنسان is an imperfect verb and its agent; the object of يريد is omitted. The meaning is: rather, man wants to remain and persist in his state of not being bound by the bond of faith, so that he may run on in his wickedness and continue in his error. The lām is for reason (taʿlīl); يفجر is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن concealed after the lām of reason, whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو, referring to man. أمامه is an adverb of place borrowed for time, i.e. so that he may continue in his wickedness and persist in it in the times before him and the time that faces him, not desisting from it nor disowning it. The lām of reason is attached to يريد. Al-Jalāl and others parsed it another way, the gist of which is that the lām is redundant (zāʾida) and يفجر is accusative by an implied أن, the maṣdar formed from it and أن being the object of يريد. There is no call for making the lām redundant, so the first view is the correct one.
(يَسْئَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيامَةِ): the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. he wants to continue in his wickedness while asking, by way of mockery, "when is the Day of Resurrection?". It has also been said to be resumptive. Abū al-Baqāʾ said it is an explanation of ليفجر, so it is explicative and resumptive, or a substitute for the clause before it, since explanation may be by resumption or by substitution. أيان is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of time, attached to an omitted element in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, and يوم القيامة is a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ): the fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is an adverb (ẓarf) for future time attached to the apodosis, which is يقول; the clause برق البصر is a verbal clause in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it.
(وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ): conjoined to برق البصر; it is a past verb and its agent.
(وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ): also conjoined, falling within the scope of the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ). Their being brought together is one of the greatest signs of Allah.
(يَقُولُ الْإِنْسانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ): the clause يقول الإنسان has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. يوم is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to يقول, and the tanwīn compensates for a clause, i.e. "on the day when the sight is dazzled, etc.". أين is an interrogative noun in the position of accusative as an adverb of place, the adverb being attached to an omitted element in the position of nominative as a fronted khabar, and المفر is a postponed mubtadaʾ. المفر is a mīmī maṣdar meaning "fleeing", or a noun of place for fleeing; the first has fatḥa on the fāʾ and the second kasra, and it has been read both ways.
(كَلَّا لا وَزَرَ): كلا is a particle of deterrence and rebuke against seeking flight; لا is the lā of generic negation; وزر is its noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, and its khabar is omitted, i.e. "existing, available to them".
(إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ):
إلى ربك is a fronted khabar; يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to an implied verb indicated by المستقر, i.e. "the matter settles with your Lord on the day when these mentioned things happen". It may not be attached to المستقر, because if it is a maṣdar, [it cannot govern] because [the adverb] precedes it, and if it is a noun of place, it has no governing power at all. المستقر is a postponed mubtadaʾ.
(يُنَبَّؤُا الْإِنْسانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِما قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ):
The clause is explicative and resumptive, as stated before. ينبأ is a passive imperfect verb; الإنسان is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, attached to ينبأ; بما is in the position of the second object; the clause قدم together with أخر conjoined to it has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. That is: man will be informed, on the day when these three things happen — the dazzling of sight, the eclipsing of the moon and the bringing together of the sun and the moon — of what he put forward, of deeds he did, and of what he held back, of deeds he did not do.
(بَلِ الْإِنْسانُ عَلى نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ):
بل is a conjunction and transitional digression; الإنسان is a mubtadaʾ; على نفسه is attached to بصيرة. As for بصيرة, it may be the khabar of الإنسان, which is the preferable view, the meaning being: rather man is a clear witness (بصيرة) against himself.
On this view the following question arises: why was the khabar made feminine? The grammarians differed in answering. Some said the hāʾ in it is not for the feminine but for intensiveness. Al-Akhfash said: it is like your saying "so-and-so is a lesson (عبرة) and a proof (حجة)". It has also been said that what is meant by man is his limbs, as though He said: rather his limbs are بصيرة, i.e. witnessing. بصيرة may also be a postponed mubtadaʾ with على نفسه a fronted khabar, the clause being a khabar about الإنسان; on this view بصيرة is an adjective of something omitted, i.e. "a seeing eye" or "limbs", and the tāʾ on this view is for the feminine. Al-Zamakhsharī took this view and said: «بصيرة: a clear proof, described with seeing figuratively, as the signs were described with seeing in His saying: فلما جاءتهم آياتنا مبصرة; or for seeing eyes». It may also be that على نفسه is the khabar and بصيرة an agent of it, the norm for predicates being the singular. The three views are equal in strength and preferability.
(وَلَوْ أَلْقى مَعاذِيرَهُ):
The wāw is circumstantial, [introducing a ḥāl] from the agent latent in بصيرة. لو is conditional; ألقى is a past verb, which is the protasis, whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو; معاذيره is a direct object. The apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e. "they would not be accepted, nor received". المعاذير is the plural of معذرة, irregularly, like ملاقيح and مذاكير, plurals of لقحة and ذكر. The grammarians have two views on this and its like: first, that it is the plural of the uttered word, i.e. لقحة; second, that it is the plural of an unuttered, implied word, i.e. ملقحة and مذكار. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: is not the regular plural of معذرة معاذر, [not] معاذير? I say: المعاذير is not a plural of معذرة but a collective noun of it; similar is المناكير for المنكر». Abū Ḥayyān said in comment: «This form is not one of the forms of collective nouns; it is one of the forms of the broken plural, so it is like مذاكير and ملاميح, the singulars of which are لمحة and ذكر, and no one has held that they are collective nouns. It has been said that they are irregular plurals of لمحة and ذكر, or that they are plurals of an unuttered singular, namely مذكار and ملمحة».
(لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ):
The clause is the object of an omitted, resumptive saying. لا is prohibitive; تحرك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا; به is attached to تحرك; لسانك is a direct object. The lām is the lām of reason; تعجل is an imperfect verb, accusative by أن concealed after the lām of reason, and the lām and what lies within its scope are attached to تحرك; به is attached to تعجل. The pronoun is for the Qurʾān, i.e. reciting and memorizing it in haste lest it escape you. Then He gave the reason for the prohibition of haste by His saying: إن علينا جمعه. إنّ, its fronted khabar and its postponed noun; قرآنه is conjoined to جمعه.
(فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ):
The fāʾ is a conjunction; إذا is an adverb for future time, and its clause قرأناه is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The fāʾ links the apodosis of إذا; اتبع is an imperative verb whose agent is latent, its implied form being أنت, and قرآنه is a direct object, i.e. be following behind in it and do not keep pace with it [Translator's note: i.e. do not recite along with the angel], and set your mind at rest that it will not remain unpreserved.
(ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; علينا is the fronted khabar of إنّ and بيانه the postponed noun of إنّ.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لا أقسم بيوم القيامة ولا أقسم بالنفس اللوّامة» there is the device of «ṣiḥḥat al-aqsām» (soundness of the oaths), which the author of al-Mathal al-Sāʾir called «correspondence between meanings». Many examples of it have passed in this book, and we have spoken about it at length. The verse before us is counted among the beauties of division, because of the correspondence of the two things sworn by: He swore first by the Day of Resurrection and then swore by the souls that will be requited on it, upon the reality of resurrection and requital. Glory be to the One who spoke this speech.

dervis-irab:20-40.t:
* Vocabulary:
(ناضِرَةٌ): from النضرة: beautiful and radiant. النضرة is living in comfort, and from it غصن ناضر (a fresh branch). One says نضر ينضر of the class of دخل, نضر ينضر of the class of تعب, and نضر ينضر of the class of ظرف, نضرا, نضرة, نضرا, نضورا and نضارة: the face, the colour, the tree or other things became soft and fine and beautiful, so it is ناضر, نضر and نضير. And أنضر is said of the stick (العود) too. Al-Kumayt said:
ورت بك عيدان المكارم كلها ... وأورق عودي في ثراك وأنضرا
(Through you all the fire-sticks of noble deeds have kindled, and my branch has leafed and grown fresh in your soil.)
In al-Asās: «She has a bracelet of نضر and نضار, which is gold; it has been said that every pure thing, of gold or other, is نضار. And a cup of نضار, which is a tamarisk of wars-yellow [Translator's note: ورسيّ, saffron-like] colour in the lowland of the Ḥijāz. Among the figurative uses: نضر وجهه: his face became beautiful and fresh; a fresh, radiant girl; a fresh boy: radiant. نضّر الله وجهه and أنضره: He made it beautiful; and sometimes نضَره is said without doubling, with وجه منضور, but that is not so good. He said:
نضّر الله أعظما دفنوها ... بسجستان طلحة الطلحات
(May Allah make radiant the bones they buried in Sijistān — Ṭalḥat al-Ṭalaḥāt.)
In the ḥadīth: «May Allah make radiant the one who heard my saying and retained it». نجار نضار: pure stock. Al-Afwah said:
كرم الفعل إذا ما فعلوا ... ونجار في اليمانين نضار
(Noble in deed whenever they act, and of pure stock among the Yemenis.)»
(فاقِرَةٌ): a great calamity that breaks the back, or its vertebrae (فقاره). الفقار is with fatḥa on the fāʾ, as in al-Qāmūs, and it is the plural of فقارة with fatḥa on the fāʾ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «فقرت الداهية الرجل فقرا, of the class of قتل: the calamity befell him, so he is فقير, فعيل in the sense of مفعول. فقارة الظهر, with fatḥa, is the vertebra, and the plural is فقار with the hāʾ dropped, like سحابة and سحاب. Ibn al-Sikkīt said: one does not say فِقارة with kasra. الفقرة is a dialectal variant of الفقارة, and its plural is فقر and فقرات, like سدرة, سدر and سدرات». In al-Qāmūs: «الفِقر, with kasra, and الفَقرة and الفَقارة, both with fatḥa: what is joined of the bones of the spine from the withers to the coccyx».
(التَّراقِيَ): plural of الترقوة, which is the bone at the top of the chest between the hollow of the throat and the shoulder; there are two collarbones, and the plural is التراقي and الترائق [Translator's note: the source has الترايق]. One says ترقاه ترقاة, i.e. he struck his collarbone; and "his soul has reached the collarbones" when he is near death.
(راقٍ):
An active participle, either from رقى — with fatḥa in the past and kasra in the imperfect — from الرقية, which is speech prepared for seeking a cure, with which the sick person is treated by incantation so that he may be healed; in the ḥadīth: "And what made you know that it is a ruqya?", meaning al-Fātiḥa, and this is one of its names. Or from رقي — with kasra in the past and fatḥa in the imperfect — from الرقي, which is ascending, i.e. the angels say: who will ascend with this soul?
(يَتَمَطَّى): imperfect of تمطّى. There are two views on it. The first is that it is from المطا, which is the back, and its meaning is "to strut", i.e. he stretches his back and twists it in swaggering as he walks. The second is that its origin is يتمطط, from تمطط, i.e. stretched himself; its meaning is that he stretches himself in his walk out of swaggering, and that is a concomitant of swaggering, so it is near to the meaning of the first but differs from it in its root, since the root of المطا is م ط و and the root of the second is م ط ط; the second ṭāʾ was changed to yāʾ only out of dislike for the gathering of like letters. المطيطاء is swaggering and stretching the arms while walking, and المطيط is the thick water at the bottom of the trough, because it stretches out in it. In the ḥadīth: "When my community walks with a swagger (المطيطاء), and Persia and Rome serve them, their might will be set among themselves." In the books of language: among figurative uses is تمطّى الليل when the night grows long. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
فقلت له لما تمطى بصلبه ... وأردف إعجازا وناء بكلكل
(I said to it, when it stretched out its back, followed with its hindquarters and rose heavily with its breast.)
And Bayhas said:
كلما قلت قد تقضّى تمطّى ... حالك اللون دامسا يحموما
(Whenever I say it has ended, it stretches out — jet-coloured, pitch-dark, black.)
(سُدىً): neglected, not charged with the laws. One says إبل سدى, i.e. left untended; and أسديت حاجتي, i.e. I let it go to waste. The meaning of أسدى إليه معروفا (he did him a kindness) is that he made it like something lost with the one to whom it was done, not mentioning it nor reminding him of it as a favour. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «السدى, on the measure of الحصى, of a cloth is the opposite of the weft (اللحمة); it is the warp stretched lengthwise in weaving. أسديت الثوب: I set up its warp. السدى is also the dew of the night, by which crops live; سديت الأرض, so it is سدية, of the class of تعب: its dew became abundant. سدا الرجل سدوا, of the class of قال: he stretched his hand towards something; سدا البعير سدوا [Translator's note: the source has «وسدّ البعير»]: he stretched his foreleg in going; أسديته with alif: I left it سدى, i.e. neglected; and أسديت إليه معروفا: I placed a kindness with him».
In al-Lisān, al-Asās and others: «A neglected camel (جمل سدى) and neglected camels; a people left to themselves; land left untilled. And السندي [Translator's note: so in the source, apparently a corruption of الندى] and السدى fell, which is what falls by night. This cloth: its warp is silk. أسديته; the weaver أسدى the cloth and سدّاه. Among figurative uses: "you have set the warp, so put in the weft; you have saddled, so bridle"; أسدى إليه معروفا; سدّى منطقا حسنا (he wove fine speech); and the slanderers سدّوا against him. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
وإنّا لمحقوقون أن لا تردّنا ... أقاويل ما سدّوا علينا ولصّقوا
(We are surely bound not to be turned back by the sayings they wove and pinned upon us.)
أسدى بين القوم: he made peace among them. "You are neither weft nor warp": you neither harm nor benefit. The wind weaves (تسدي) the waymarks and wefts (تنير) them. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
لمن الديار كأنهنّ سطور ... تسدي معالمها الصبا وتنير
(Whose are the dwellings, as though they were lines of writing, whose traces the east wind warps and wefts?)
تسدّاه: he rose over him and seized him from above, as the dew of the night does. He said:
وما أبو سمرة بالرث ألوان ... يوم تسدى الحكم بن مروان
(Abū Samra is not shabby in colours, on the day he came down upon al-Ḥakam ibn Marwān.)
That is, he seized him by his forelock while he was on a horse».
(تَمَنَّى): it is poured into the womb. المني is the gushing fluid that comes out in intercourse.

* I'rab:
(كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعاجِلَةَ): [كلا] is a particle of deterrence and rebuke; بل is a transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī); تحبون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent). The address is to the disbelievers of Quraysh and to man in general. It was read with tāʾ, by way of iltifāt (shift of address), and with yāʾ, in the third person. العاجلة is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. this world.
(وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ): conjoined to the previous clause; it was also read with tāʾ and yāʾ, as above.
(وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ): وجوه is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ناضرة an adjective of it; يومئذ is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by ناضرة; إلى ربها is attached (mutaʿalliq) to ناظرة, and ناظرة is the khabar (predicate) of وجوه. The meaning is that the beautiful faces on the Day of Resurrection are looking at their Lord. This is a sound meaning and an easy analysis. وجوه may also be a mubtadaʾ with ناضرة its khabar, يومئذ being an adverb made accusative by ناضرة; beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted here because the place is a place of detailing. ناظرة then is an adjective of وجوه, or a second khabar, or the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; إلى ربها is attached to ناظرة. يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, and the tanwīn compensates for a clause, i.e. "on the day when the Resurrection takes place". More discussion of these two verses will come in the Benefits section.
(وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ باسِرَةٌ تَظُنُّ أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِها فاقِرَةٌ): conjoined to what precedes, and the i'rab has been discussed. It must be pointed out that يومئذ does not specify the indefinite noun so as to permit beginning with it, because an adverb of time cannot be an adjective of a concrete thing; it is only governed by باسرة, as we said it is governed by ناضرة above. The clause تظن may be the khabar on the first view, or a khabar after a khabar. أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of تظن; بها is attached to يفعل, and فاقرة is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of يفعل. The meaning of ظن here is certainty, or expectation with a predominant conviction, because it is the time when doubts are lifted.
(كَلَّا إِذا بَلَغَتِ التَّراقِيَ): كلا is a deterrent from preferring this world to the Hereafter, and a reminder to them of the death they will come to, at which the transitory world is cut off and one passes from it to the deferred one. إذا is an adverb for future time; the clause بلغت is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. The agent of بلغت is latent (mustatir), its implied form being هي, referring to the soul, which the context of the speech indicates even though it has not been mentioned, as Ḥātim said:
أماويّ ما يغني الثراء عن الفتى ... إذا حشرجت يوما وضاق بها الصدر
(O Māwiyya, of what use is wealth to a young man when one day it rattles in the throat and the breast grows tight with it?)
The Arabs say أرسلت ("it sent down"), meaning "the rain came", and you hardly ever hear them mention the sky. التراقي is a direct object.
(وَقِيلَ مَنْ راقٍ):
The wāw is a conjunction; قيل is a passive past verb, and its deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. those around him [Translator's note: so in the source]. من is an interrogative noun in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and راق is its khabar; it is nominative, the sign of its nominative being the implied ḍamma on the yāʾ that was omitted because of the meeting of two vowelless letters. The clause من راق is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). I do not know the meaning of al-Samīn's statement: «This clause is the one standing in place of the agent».
(وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ الْفِراقُ): the wāw is a conjunction; ظن is a past verb meaning "he was certain". Certainty was called ظن because as long as a person's soul is in his body he hopes for the continuance of life, out of his intense love of it and attachment to it. أنّ and its noun, and the ẓarf [Translator's note: so in the source; الفراق is in fact the khabar] is its khabar; أنّ and what lies within its scope are in the position of accusative, filling the place of the two objects of ظن.
(وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ): also conjoined; more on its meaning will come in the Rhetoric section.
(إِلى رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَساقُ): the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element which is a fronted khabar; يومئذ is an adverb attached to المساق, annexed to its like, and the tanwīn compensates for four clauses: the soul has reached the collarbones; it is said, who is a healer; he is certain it is the parting; and the shank is wrapped with the shank. المساق is a postponed mubtadaʾ. The apodosis of إذا, which is what governs it, is indicated by His saying إلى ربك يومئذ المساق, i.e. it will be driven to the judgement and will of its Lord. المساق is مَفعَل from السوق, so it is a quasi-maṣdar (ism maṣdar).
(فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى): conjoined to His saying أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه. لا is negative; صدق is a past verb — this is evidence that the negative لا may enter the past tense — whose agent is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. man. ولا صلى is conjoined to فلا صدق. It has also been said to be conjoined to the clause يسأل أيان يوم القيامة.
(وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى): also conjoined. لكن is lightened and inoperative; كذب is a past verb, i.e. man, and تولى is conjoined to it.
(ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلى أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّى): ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; the secret of it is finding it far-fetched, because whoever has done such a thing ought to fear the descent of Allah's anger, and so walk fearful and subdued; yet this man walks strutting and haughty, vying with the reaches of the sky in height, though he is of lower worth and baser station. إلى أهله is attached to ذهب, and the clause يتمطى is circumstantial (ḥāliyya) from the agent of ذهب.
(أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى): discussion of the i'rab of this word was given at length in Sūrat al-Qitāl.
(ثُمَّ أَوْلى لَكَ فَأَوْلى): conjoined to what precedes; the repetition is for emphasis and increase of the threat. Al-Khansāʾ clung to the fringes of this repetition and said:
هممت بنفسي كل الهموم ... فأولى لنفسي أولى لها
(I resolved upon my own life every resolve — so woe to my soul, woe to it.)
(أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدىً): the hamza is for a question of denial; يحسب الإنسان is a verb and its agent; أن and what lies within its scope fill the place of the two objects of يحسب. The deputy agent is latent, its implied form being هو. سدى is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in يترك.
(أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنى): the hamza is for a question of affirmation and denial; لم is a particle of negation, inversion [to the past] and jussive; يك is a deficient (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, the sign of its jussive being the implied sukūn on the nūn omitted for lightening. The noun of يك is latent, its implied form being هو, i.e. man; نطفة is its khabar; من مني is an adjective; the clause يمنى, in the passive, is an adjective of مني. It was also read with tāʾ.
(ثُمَّ كانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّى): conjoined to what precedes. The conjunction is with ثم for delay and length of time, because between the second creation, which is the creation of offspring, and the first creation there is delay and a long span, so it had to be conjoined with ثم. كان and its latent noun, and علقة is its khabar. The two fāʾs are for sequence with immediacy.
(فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثى): also conjoined, with immediacy. جعل is a past verb; منه is in the position of the second object; الزوجين is the first object of جعل; الذكر is a badal (substitute) and الأنثى is conjoined to it.
(أَلَيْسَ ذلِكَ بِقادِرٍ عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى): the hamza is for a question of denial and affirmation; ذلك is the noun of ليس, i.e. the doer [of these things]; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and قادر is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس; على أن يحيي الموتى is attached to قادر.

* Rhetoric:
1- The representational metaphor (istiʿāra tamthīliyya) in His saying «والتفّت الساق بالساق»: a representational metaphor for the severity of the distress of this world on its last day and the severity of the distress of the Hereafter on its first day, because they are two days that have wrapped around each other and become mixed with distress, as the shank wraps around the shank — as it is said, "war has bared its shank", a metaphor for its severity. It has also been said that their wrapping is from the severity of the illness, because it contracts and extends and lays this one over that. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «His shank wrapped around his shank and twisted over it in the agony (عَلَز) of death», which is the trembling that seizes the sick person.
2- In His saying «والتفّت الساق بالساق إلى ربك يومئذ المساق» there is the incomplete paronomasia (al-tajnīs al-nāqiṣ), also called jinās al-tabdīl. It is that in one of the two words there is a letter not found in the other, while all the letters of the other are found in its sister in their order. It has three divisions: a division in which the addition occurs at the beginning of the word, like the addition of the mīm in المساق; a division in which the addition occurs in the middle of the word, as in His saying, the Exalted: وإنه على ذلك لشهيد وإنه لحب الخير لشديد; and a division in which the addition occurs at the end of the word, as in His saying, the Exalted: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات.

* Benefits:
We will not dwell long on the question of the vision of Allah the Exalted on the Day of Resurrection, for it is a question treated in the principles of religion (uṣūl al-dīn), and the proofs of the two ways, the people of the Sunna and the Muʿtazila, are well known. Since al-Zamakhsharī was of the Muʿtazila, and his doctrine is that fronting the object indicates restriction (ikhtiṣāṣ), he said concerning His saying, the Exalted, «إلى ربها ناظرة»: «It is known that they will look at things beyond enumeration and not falling under number, in a place of gathering where all creatures are assembled; so restricting their looking to Him, were He someone looked at, is impossible. It must therefore be taken in a sense with which the restriction is valid; and what is valid with it is that it be from people's saying: "I am looking to so-and-so (أنا إلى فلان ناظر), what he will do for me", intending the sense of expectation and hope. From it is the poet's saying:
وإذا نظرت إليك من ملك ... والبحر دونك زدتني نعما
(Whenever I looked to you, O king — and the sea is less than you — you increased me in favours.)
I heard a woman of the Sarāt begging in Mecca at midday, when people shut their doors and retire to their resting places, saying: "My little eyes are looking to Allah and to you." The meaning is that they expect favour and honour only from their Lord, as they were in this world, fearing none and hoping in none but Him». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «They — meaning the Muʿtazila — held that the meaning is "looking to the mercy of their Lord", or to His reward or His dominion; so they implied an omitted muḍāf. This is a permissible approach in Arabic, as you say "so-and-so is looking to you in such-and-such", i.e. to your doing».
Ibn al-Munayyir, as is his custom, commented on al-Zamakhsharī and said: «How short his tongue is at this verse! How long he hums and expatiates in denying the vision, splitting hairs [lit. "splitting the cloak"], multiplying words and going deep; yet when this verse opened its mouth, all he did in his silence [Translator's note: so in the source; the wording appears disturbed] was to argue that, had vision been meant, it would not have been restricted by the fronting of the object, because it would then not be restricted on the assumption of the vision of Allah the Exalted. He does not know that the one who enjoys the vision of the beauty of the Face of Allah the Exalted will not turn his glance away from it, nor prefer another to it, nor set any other object of sight beside Him, Mighty and Majestic; and it is fitting that he should restrict his vision to the One like whom there is nothing. We see the lover in this world: when you grant him sight of his beloved, he will not turn from him for a moment nor prefer anything to him — so how about the lover of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, if he were to miss looking at His Noble Face? We ask Allah the Great not to turn His Face away from us, and to protect us from the slippery places of innovation and the stumbles of doubt; He is sufficient for us, and the best Disposer of affairs».

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ [فَٱتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ]﴾.
When Gabriel, peace be upon him, recites it to you, "فاتبع قرآنه" (then follow its recitation). القراءة and القرآن are both maṣdars (verbal nouns), just as you say: راجحٌ بيِّن الرجحان والرجوح (clearly preponderant, رجحان and رجوح), and المعرفة and العرفان, and الطواف and الطوفان.

farraa:20-21.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ﴾. ﴿وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلآخِرَةَ﴾.
It has been transmitted from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah have mercy on him: "بَلْ تُحِبُّون، وتَذَرُون" with tāʾ, and many read it "بل يحبون" with yāʾ. The Qur'an sometimes addresses those to whom it was sent down directly, and at other times treats them as absent, as in His saying: ﴿حَتَّى إِذَا كُنْتُمْ فى الْفُلْكِ وجَرَيْنَ بِهِمْ بِرِيحٍ طَيِّبَةٍ﴾.

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وُجُوهٌ يُوْمَئِذٍ نَّاضِرَةٌ﴾.
Radiant with bliss.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَظُنُّ أَن يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ﴾.
الفاقرة is the calamity (الداهية). The names of the Resurrection and of the punishment have come with the meanings of calamities and with their names.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ إِذَا بَلَغَتِ ٱلتَّرَاقِيَ﴾.
He says: when a man's soul reaches his collarbones (تراقيه) at death, and those around him say: "مَنْ رَاقٍ؟" — is there [any] healer? Is there any charmer (راق)? — and the man thinks "أنه الفراق", i.e. he knows that it is the parting. It is also said: "Is there any راق" because the Angel of Death has angels with him, and when the dying man gives up [117/a] his soul, some of them say to others: "Which of you will ascend (يرقى) with it?" — from رقيت, meaning: I ascended.

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ﴾.
The first hardship of the affair of the Hereafter came upon him together with the hardest, last part of the affair of this world; that is His saying: ﴿وَٱلْتَفَّتِ ٱلسَّاقُ بِٱلسَّاقِ﴾. It is also said: his two shanks were wound together, just as it is said of a woman whose thighs touch each other: she is لَفّاء.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَتَمَطَّىٰ﴾.
He struts; because the back is the مَطا, so he twists his back in strutting. This is specifically about Abū Jahl.

farraa:37-37.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مِّن مَّنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ﴾.
With yāʾ and with tāʾ. Whoever says يُمنَى refers it to the مني (semen), and تُمنى refers it to the نطفة (drop). Both are correct. The companions of ʿAbdullāh [ibn Masʿūd] read it with tāʾ, and some of the people of Medina [also] with tāʾ.

farraa:40-40.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن يُحْيِـيَ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ﴾.
You pronounce both yāʾs distinctly, giving the first a kasra, with the ḥāʾ vowelless. If you give the ḥāʾ a kasra and transfer to it the vowel of the first yāʾ that follows it, that is correct, as the poet said:
وكأنها بين النساء سبيكة * تمشى بِسُدَّةِ بيتها فتَعَىّ
(As though, among the women, she were an ingot [of silver], walking in the porch of her house and growing weary.)
He meant: فتعيا.

farraa:1-1.t:
Abū ʿAbd Allāh said: I heard al-Farrāʾ say: His saying: ﴿لاَ أُقْسِمُ﴾ — many of the grammarians used to say: (لا) is a connective (ṣila, i.e. redundant). Al-Farrāʾ said: One does not begin with a negation and then make it a connective intended to be discarded; for if this were permitted, a statement containing a negation could not be distinguished from a statement containing none. Rather, the Qur'an came as a rebuttal of those who denied the Resurrection, Paradise and the Fire, so the oath came as a rebuttal of them in much speech, both what begins [a discourse] and what does not — like your saying in speech: لا والله لا أفعل ذاك (No, by Allah, I will not do that). They made (لا), even when you see it at the beginning, a rejection of speech that has preceded. If you dropped (لا) from what is intended as a reply, there would be no difference between an oath that is a reply and an oath that begins afresh. Do you not see that you say, beginning: والله إن الرسول لحق (By Allah, the Messenger is true); but when you say: لا والله إن الرسول لحق (No, by Allah, the Messenger is true), it is as if you were giving the lie to people who denied it? This is the aspect of (لا) with oaths, and with all oaths in every place where you see (لا) placed at the beginning; and it is frequent in speech.
Someone who did not know this aspect, as you see [115/a], used to read: "لأقسم بيوم القيامة" — it is reported of al-Ḥasan — making it a lām prefixed to أقسم; and that is correct, because the Arabs say: لأحلف بالله ليكونن كذا وكذا (I shall swear by Allah that such and such will surely happen), making it a lām without the meaning of لا.
[Translator's note: «هذا الوجاز» is as printed, evidently for «هذا جاز» ("this were permitted").]

farraa:10-10.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيْنَ ٱلْمَفَرُّ﴾.
The people read المفر with fatḥa on the fāʾ. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] And he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Yaḥyā ibn Salama ibn Kuhayl told me, from his father, from a man, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "أين المفِر", and said: المفَر is only the flight-place of the animal, where it flees. They are two dialect forms: المفِر and المفَر, المدِبّ and المدَبّ. Whatever has a kasra in its yafʿilu form, like يدِب, يفِر and يصِح, the Arabs say [its noun of place as]: مَفِر and مفَر, مصِح and مَصَح, مَدِب and مَدَب. One of them recited to me:
كأن بقَايا الأثر فوقَ متونه * مَدب الدَّبى فوق النقا وهو سارِح
(As if the traces of the [sword's] grain on its blades were the creeping-track of young locusts over the sand-dune as they roam.)
They recite it مَدَب, which is more frequent than مَدِب. One says: جاء على مَدَب السيل and مدِب السيل (he came along the flood's course), and ما فى قميصه مَصِح ولا مَصَحٌّ (there is no sound place in his shirt).

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَلاَّ لاَ وَزَرَ﴾.
الوزر is a refuge.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُنَبَّأُ ٱلإِنسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ﴾.
He means: what he sent ahead of his deeds, and what he left behind of a practice (sunna) that he left to be acted upon after him. If he established a good practice, he has the like [of the reward] of those who act on it, without their being diminished; and if it was an evil practice, he is punished for it, without anything being diminished from the punishment of those who act on it.
[Translator's note: «بعمل بها» is as printed, for «يُعمل بها» ("to be acted upon").]

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلِ ٱلإِنسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ﴾.
He is saying: over man there are watchers from his own self who bear witness against him about his deeds: the hands, the feet, the eyes and the private part. The poet said:
كأنَّ على ذى الظن عيناً بصيرةً * بمقعَدِه أو منظرٍ هو ناظرُه
يُحاذِرُ حتى يحسِبُ الناسَ كلَّهم * من الخوفِ لا تخفى عليهم سرائرُه
(It is as if over the suspicious man there were a watchful eye, at his seat or at any sight he beholds; he is so wary that out of fear he reckons all people to be people from whom his secrets are not hidden.)

farraa:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ﴾.
It has come in the interpretation: even if he lets down his curtains. And it has come: even if he makes excuses, there is over him one who will give the lie to his excuse.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying [116/b], Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ﴾.
When Jibrīl ﷺ came down with the revelation to Muḥammad ﷺ with the Qur'an, he would recite part of it to himself before it was complete, for fear of forgetting it. So it was said to him: ﴿لاَ تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ﴾ in your heart ﴿وَقُرْآنَهُ﴾ and its recitation; i.e. Jibrīl, peace be upon him, will repeat it to you.
[Translator's note: the one who "would recite part of it to himself" is the Prophet ﷺ, as the address that follows shows.]

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ أُقْسِمُ بِٱلنَّفْسِ ٱللَّوَّامَةِ﴾.
There is no soul, righteous or wicked, but that it blames itself: if it has done good, it says: Why did I not do more? And if it has done evil, it says: Would that I had held back! Would that I had not done it!

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَن نُّسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ﴾.
It has come in the interpretation: Yes, We are able to make his fingertips even, i.e. to make his fingers solid, not separated, like a camel's hoof. So He said: Yes, [We are] able to restore the smallest bones as they were. His saying "قادرين" is accusative as departing from "نجمع" [i.e. as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the subject of نجمع], as if you said in speech: أتحسب أن لن نقوى عليك، بلى قادرين على أقوى منك (Do you think we will not overpower you? Yes, [we are] able [to overpower] one stronger than you). He means: yes, we will overpower, being able; yes, we will overpower, being capable of more than this. Had it been nominative as a fresh start, as if He said: بلى نحن قادرون على أكثر من ذا (yes, We are able to do more than this), it would be correct.
As for people's saying: [the underlying form is] بلى نقدر, and when it was turned into قادرين it became accusative — that is a mistake, because a verb is not made accusative by converting it from yafʿalu to fāʿil. Do you not see that you say: أتقوم إلينا (will you rise to [come to] us?), and if you convert it to the fāʿil form you say: أقائم, and it would be a mistake to say: أقائماً أنت إِلينا؟ They used to cite as proof the saying of al-Farazdaq:
على قسَمٍ لا أشتم الدهر مسلما * ولا خارجا مِنْ فىَّ زورُ كلام
(Upon an oath that I will never revile a Muslim, nor shall false speech come out of my mouth.)
They said: he only meant لا أشتم and ولا يخرج, and when he turned it into خارج he made it accusative. But he made it accusative only because he meant: عاهدتُ ربى لا شاتما أحدا ولا خارجاً من فىّ زور كلام (I have pledged to my Lord, not reviling anyone and no false speech coming out of my mouth). And his saying لا أشتم is in the position of the accusative [115/b].

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from Abū Ḥaṣīn, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ ٱلإِنسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ﴾; he said: He says: I will repent later, I will repent later. And al-Kalbī said: he multiplies sins and puts off repentance.

farraa:7-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا بَرِقَ ٱلْبَصَرُ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash, ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and some of the people of Medina read it (بَرِق) with kasra on the rāʾ, and Nāfiʿ al-Madanī read it: "فإِذ بَرَق البصر" with fatḥa on the rāʾ, from البريق (glitter): it stares, for whoever reads with fatḥa. And his saying "بَرِق" [means]: it is terrified. One of the Arabs recited to me:
نَعَانِى حَنانةُ طُوبالةً * تُسَفُّ يَبيسًا من العِشْرِقِ
فنفسَكَ فَانْعَ ولا تَنْعَنِى * وداوِ الكُلُومَ ولا تَبْرَقِ
(Ḥanāna announced my death — a ewe fed on dry ʿishriq. Announce your own death, not mine; treat the wounds and do not be terrified.)
He gave the rāʾ fatḥa, i.e.: do not be terrified by the horror of the wounds you have; likewise the sight will be terrified on the Day of Resurrection.
And whoever reads "بَرَق" says: he opened his eyes [wide]; and his sight also glitters because of that.
[Translator's note: «فإِذ» is as printed (for «فإذا»), and «بَرق» glossed as "terrified" is to be read بَرِق. «تَبْرَقِ» in the verse is the imperfect of بَرِق, hence "he gave the rāʾ fatḥa". «يرق بصره» is as printed, for «برق بصره» ("his sight glitters").]

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَخَسَفَ ٱلْقَمَرُ﴾.
Its light has gone.

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجُمِعَ ٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ﴾.
[In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh:] وجمع بين الشمس والقمر — He means: [joined] also in the loss of their light, so there is no light for this one nor for that one. Its meaning is: He joined them together in the loss of light, as you say: هذا يوم يستوى فيه الأعمى والبصير (this is a day in which the blind and the seeing are equal), i.e. both of them are blind in it. It is also said: they are brought together like two hamstrung bulls in the Fire. He said جُمِع and did not say جمعت for this reason: because the meaning is "He joined between them"; this is one way. Or, if you wish, you may take both of them in the sense of two lights, as if you said: the two lights were joined, the two radiances were joined; that is the view of al-Kisāʾī. Some people used to say: the verb of the sun was made masculine only because it is not singled out by [the verb] جُمع until something else shares it; so when a masculine noun shares it, the expression for both is جُمِعا, and جمعتا is not used. It was said to them: How do you say "the sun [116/a] was joined, and the moon"? They said: جُمِعت; and so they retracted that view.
[Translator's note: «ثورين» ("two bulls") in «فى مذهب ثورين» is as printed; the sense requires «نورين» ("two lights"), which is how the following sentence explains it.]

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «لا» is the negative [lā] for emphasising the oath; one does not swear by a thing except to magnify it.

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «أن» is lightened, and its noun is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); the clause «لن نجمع» is the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; «أن» with what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), stands in place of the two objects of «حسب».

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: «بلى» is a particle of answer; «قادرين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) verb, i.e.: We will gather them, being able; the maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن نُسَوِّي» is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادرين»; and the implied clause «نجمعها» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «يريد» is resumptive, and the object of «يريد» is omitted, i.e.: his desires; the genitive maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليفجر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يريد»; «أمامه» is an adverb [of place] borrowed here for time.

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «يسأل» is a badal (substitute) from the clause {يُرِيدُ}; «أيان» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «يوم»; the clause «أيان يوم» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the asking.

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The fāʾ is resumptive; «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) {يَقُولُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يقول»; «إذٍ» is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «أين» is an interrogative noun, an adverb of place attached to the khabar (predicate); «المفر» is a mubtadaʾ (subject).

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: (كلا لا وزر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The khabar (predicate) of the lā of generic negation is implied (muqaddar), i.e.: existing (موجود), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: (إلى ربك يومئذ المستقر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «المستقر»; «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to the [notion of] being-settled (al-istiqrār) to which the khabar is attached; and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: The clause «ينبَّأ» is resumptive, and the adverb is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينبأ».

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: (بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive; the preposition phrase «على نفسه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بصيرة», and the tāʾ in «بصيرة» is for intensification.

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: (ولو ألقى معاذيره) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in {بَصِيرَةٌ}; the wāw conjoins this ḥāl to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl, i.e.: a witness against himself in every state, even in this state; this is for exhaustiveness; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: they would not be accepted from him.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: (إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: (فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The first fāʾ is parenthetical; the fāʾ in «فاتبع» is [that of] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); «قرآنه» is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the conditional clause is parenthetical.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The clause «إن علينا بيانه» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ}.

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: (كلا بل تحبون العاجلة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: «وجوه» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); «ناضرة» is a naʿt (adjective); «يومئذ» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ناضرة»; beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because the place is one of detailing and because the mubtadaʾ is qualified.

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «ناظرة» is the khabar (predicate) of {وُجُوهٌ}; the preposition phrase «إلى ربها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ناظرة».

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: (ووجوه يومئذ باسرة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] Parallel to verse (22); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاضِرَةٌ}.

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: The clause «تظن» is the khabar (predicate) of the second «وُجُوهٌ»; «أن» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «تظن», and «أنْ» governs the subjunctive (nāṣiba).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: His words «التراقي»: the object of «بلغت»; the fāʿil (agent) refers to the soul even though it has not been mentioned; «إذا» is adverbial and conditional, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ): it is driven to its Lord, and the following clause (إلى ربك المساق) indicates the apodosis.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: «من» is an interrogative noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); «راق» is the khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) with the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the omitted yāʾ, because it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ).

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: (وظن أنه الفراق) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] «أنَّ» with what follows it stands in place of the two objects of «ظن».

harrat-mujtaba:30-30.t: (إلى ربك يومئذ المساق) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is explicative of the implied (muqaddar) apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of «إذا», and the adverb «يومئذ» is a badal (substitute) from the preceding «إذا».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: (فلا صدق ولا صلى) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «كذَّب» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause before it.

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The clause «يتمطى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «ذهب».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: «أولى لك»: [«أولى»] is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition phrase is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate); «فأولى» is a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «أولى».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: «ثم» is a conjunction, and the clause «أولى لك» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: «أنْ» governs the subjunctive (nāṣiba), and the clause «يُترك» is its khabar (predicate); «أنْ» with what follows it, interpreted as a maṣdar (verbal noun), stands in place of the two objects of «حسب»; «سدى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: The preposition phrase «مِنْ منيّ» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نطفة», and the clause «يُمنى» is a naʿt of «مني».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: The preposition phrase «منه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل»; «الذكر» is a badal (substitute).

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: (أليس ذلك بقادر) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar (predicate) of ليس; the genitive interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قادر».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t:
His saying, the Exalted: (لا أقسم): (لا) is redundant (zāʾida), because it is in the status of one occurring in the middle [of speech], since the whole Qur'an was sent down at one time to the lowest heaven, and was then sent down upon the Prophet, upon him be peace, after that over twenty-odd years, as Allah willed, of what He wished to send down piece by piece. If a speaker were to begin speech, it would not be permissible for him to bring a redundant (لا) at the beginning of his speech. It is also said that (لا) is not redundant; it is only a rejection of speech that preceded in another sūra. The second (لا) is not redundant: Allah, exalted be His mention, informed us that He swore by the Day of Resurrection and that He did not swear by the self-reproaching soul. Whoever read (لأقسم) without an alif made it a lām of oath entering upon (أقسم); this is far-fetched because of the omission of the nūn, since it should properly be (لأقسمن). It was permissible with the omission here only because he made (أقسم) refer to the present; when it is present, the nūn is not obligatory in the oath, because the nūn is obligatory in most cases only to distinguish between the present and the future. It has also been said that it is for the future, but the nūn was omitted, just as they allowed omitting the lām of the oath while keeping the nūn; and they recited:
... وقتيل مرة أثأرن فإنه فرغ وإن أخاهم لم يثأر ...
(And the slain of Murra I will surely avenge, for his blood is unavenged, while their brother has not been avenged.)
Sībawayh allowed the omission of the nūn that accompanies the lām in the oath.

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (بلى قادرين): it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of an implied verb, its implied form being "Yes, We shall gather them, being able"; this is the view of Sībawayh. It is also said that (قادرين) is accusative because it occurs in the position of (نقدر), the implied form being "Yes, We are able"; when the noun was put in the place of the verb, it was made accusative. This is a view far from the correct one; it would entail the accusative of (قائم) in your saying "I passed by a standing man" (مررت برجل قائم), because it is in the position of (يقوم).

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (يسأل أيان يوم القيامة): (أيان) is an adverbial of time (ẓarf zamān) meaning "when", and it is indeclinable (mabnī). It should properly have been vowelless, but two vowelless letters met, the alif and the nūn, so the nūn was given fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, like (كيف) and (أين). Indeclinability was necessary for (أيان) only because it means (متى), so it contains the meaning of the interrogative and resembles the interrogative particle; so it was made indeclinable, since the basic state of particles is indeclinability.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (وجمع الشمس والقمر): (جمع) came in the masculine form although (الشمس) is feminine only because it is construed according to the meaning, as if He said "the two lights were gathered" or "the two luminaries"; this is the view of al-Kisāʾī. It is also said: since the implied form is "it was gathered between (بين) the sun and the moon", the verb was made masculine for the masculinity of (بين). It is also said: since the meaning is "they were gathered together", as the statement is not complete except with the moon, and the moon is masculine, the masculine prevailed, according to the origin of putting the verb after both of them. Al-Mubarrad said: since the femininity of (الشمس) is not real, the masculine is permissible in it, since femininity in this kind does not occur to distinguish between one thing and another.

mekki-muskil:10-10.t:
His saying (أين المفر): (المفر) is a maṣdar (verbal noun), so it means "where is the fleeing?"
His saying (بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة): (الإنسان) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (بصيرة) is a second mubtadaʾ, and (على نفسه) is the khabar (predicate) of (بصيرة); the clause is the khabar of (الإنسان). The precise sense of its implied form is: "Rather, over man there are watchers from himself against himself who bear witness against him." (بصيرة) may also be the khabar of (الإنسان), the hāʾ in (بصيرة) being for intensification. It is also said: since its meaning is "a proof against himself", it entered for the femininity of (الحجة) "proof".

mekki-muskil:22-22.t: His saying (وجوه يومئذ ناضرة): (وجوه) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), (ناضرة) is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and (إلى ربها ناظرة) is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ. (ناضرة) may also be the khabar and (إلى ربها ناظرة) a second khabar. (ناظرة) may also be a naʿt of (ناضرة) or of (وجوه), with (ناضرة) the khabar of (الوجوه). The entry of (إلى) with looking indicates that it is looking with the eye and not from waiting; had it been from waiting, (إلى) would not enter with it. Do you not see that you do not say "I waited to Zayd" (انتظرت إلى زيد), while you say "I looked at Zayd" (نظرت إلى زيد)? So (إلى) accompanies the looking of the eye and does not accompany the "looking" of waiting. Whoever said that (ناظرة) means "awaiting" has erred in meaning and in i'rab, and has put speech out of its place. Some of the Muʿtazila deviated at this place, and their arbitrariness and departure from the community reached the point that they said (إلى) is not a preposition but a noun, the singular of (آلاء) "favours", and (ربها) is genitive by the annexation of (إلى) to it, not by a preposition; the implied form according to him is "the favour of its Lord is awaited". This is impossible in meaning, because the Exalted said (وجوه يومئذ ناضرة), i.e. "radiant with bliss", and He has informed us that they are blissful, so bliss has entered upon them and its signs have appeared on them; how then would one await what Allah has told us is present in them? One awaits only a thing that does not exist; as for a thing that exists and is present, how is it awaited?
