Is it permissible for you to say "I am waiting for Zayd" while he is with you, has not left you, and his leaving you is not expected? This is great ignorance from the one who interprets it so. Some of the Muʿtazila held that (ناظرة) is from looking with the eye, but said that its meaning is "looking at the reward of their Lord"; this too is a departure from the apparent meaning. If this were permissible, then "I looked at Zayd" would be permissible in the sense of "I looked at Zayd's gift", and this is a breaking of the speech of the Arabs, and in it is confusion and breaking of meanings. Moreover, we say: if the matter were so, the greatest awaited reward would be looking at Him; there is no god but He.

mekki-muskil:31-31.t: His saying (فلا صدق ولا صلى): the second (لا) is negation and is not a conjunction; its meaning is "he did not believe and did not pray".

mekki-muskil:33-33.t:
His saying (يتمطى): in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in (ذهب). Its origin is (يتمطط), from (المطيطاء) "strutting", but they replaced the second ṭāʾ with a yāʾ, and it turned into an alif because it was vowelled and what precedes it had fatḥa. (التمطط) is stretching.
His saying (سدى): accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in (يترك), and (أن) [with its clause] stands in place of the two objects of (حسب).

mekki-muskil:39-39.t: His saying (الذكر والأنثى): a badal (substitute) from (الزوجين). (جعل) means "created", which is why it passes to only one object.

mekki-muskil:40-40.t: His saying (أن يحيي الموتى): assimilation in the two yāʾs is not permissible according to the grammarians, just as it is not permissible when you do not put the verb in the accusative, because if you assimilated, two vowelless letters would meet, since the second is vowelless, and the first is not assimilated until it is made vowelless. Likewise, for every letter you assimilate into a letter after it, the first must be made vowelless. They agree on disallowing assimilation in the nominative state. As for the accusative state, al-Farrāʾ allowed it because of the vowel on the second yāʾ; but it is not permissible according to the Basrans, because the vowel is incidental, not original.

muyesser-irab:27-27.t:
﴿وقيل﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «قيل» is a past verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named).
﴿من﴾: an interrogative in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ), mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿راق﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative, the sign of its nominative being the ḍamma implied (muqaddar) on the yāʾ that was elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The clause that is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:28-28.t:
﴿وظن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «ظن» is a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿أنه﴾: «أن» is an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh), and the hāʾ is its noun.
﴿الفراق﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «أن», nominative (marfūʿ); «أن» and what falls within its scope are in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ﴿ظن﴾.

muyesser-irab:29-29.t:
﴿والتفت﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «التفت» is a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine.
﴿الساق﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma.
﴿بالساق﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿التفت﴾.

muyesser-irab:30-30.t:
﴿إلى ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿يومئذ﴾: an adverb (ẓarf), attached to the omitted khabar to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; «إذٍ» is a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on a sukūn implied (muqaddar) because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of a genitive (majrūr), muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for four clauses, the implied form being: "on the day when [the soul] reaches the collarbones, and it is said 'Who is a healer?', and he is certain that it is the parting, and shank is wrapped with shank".
﴿المساق﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:31-31.t:
﴿فلا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿صدق﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he), i.e. man.
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لا» is negating.
﴿صلى﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause is conjoined to His saying: ﴿أيحسب الإنسان أن لن نجمع عظامه﴾, and it was said: conjoined to the clause ﴿يسأل أيّان يوم القيامة﴾.

muyesser-irab:32-32.t:
﴿ولكن﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «لكن» is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala).
﴿كذب﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿وتولى﴾: the wāw is a past verb [Translator's note: so in the source; evidently something has dropped out, i.e. "the wāw is a conjunction, and «تولى» is a past verb"]; its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (he), and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:33-33.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿ذهب﴾: a past verb; its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿إلى أهله﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ذهب﴾.
﴿يتمطى﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (he); the clause «يتمطى» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause from the fāʿil of ﴿ذهب﴾.

muyesser-irab:34-34.t:
﴿أولى﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿فأولى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أولى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first «أولى».

muyesser-irab:35-35.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay.
﴿أولى﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma.
﴿لك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate).
﴿فأولى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and «أولى» is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the first «أولى»,
and the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

muyesser-irab:36-36.t:
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿يترك﴾: an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named), accusative (manṣūb); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿سدى﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «يترك».

muyesser-irab:37-37.t:
﴿ألم﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation and disapproval (al-istifhām al-taqrīrī al-inkārī), and «لم» is a particle of negation, conversion [of the imperfect to past meaning], and jussive.
﴿يك﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لم﴾, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn implied (muqaddar) on the nūn that was elided for lightening; the noun of «يك» is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he), i.e. man.
﴿نطفة﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿من مني﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted naʿt (adjective).
﴿يمنى﴾: an imperfect verb, passive (built for that whose agent is not named), nominative (marfūʿ); the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being "huwa" (it), referring back to «المني»; the clause ﴿يمنى﴾ is a naʿt of ﴿مني﴾.

muyesser-irab:38-38.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence and delay.
﴿كان﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb; its noun is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "huwa" (he).
﴿علقة﴾: the khabar of kāna, accusative (manṣūb).
﴿فخلق﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence and immediate succession, and «خلق» is a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (He), i.e. Allah.
﴿فسوى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence and immediate succession, and «سوى» is a past verb; the fāʿil is "huwa" (He), i.e. Allah; and the clause is conjoined to what came before.

muyesser-irab:39-39.t:
﴿فجعل﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction for sequence and immediate succession, and «جعل» is a past verb; the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (He), i.e. Allah; and the clause is conjoined to what came before.
﴿منه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿الزوجين﴾: the first object of ﴿جعل﴾.
﴿الذكر﴾: badal (substitute), accusative (manṣūb).
﴿والأنثى﴾: conjoined to «الذكر».

muyesser-irab:40-40.t:
﴿أليس﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation (al-istifhām al-inkārī al-taqrīrī), and «ليس» is an abrogating (nāsikh) past verb.
﴿ذلك﴾: the noun of «ليس».
﴿بقادر﴾: the bāʾ is a connective (ṣila) preposition, and «قادر» is genitive in form and accusative in position, the khabar of «ليس».
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿يحيي﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb); the fāʿil (agent) is "huwa" (He); the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يحيي﴾ is a noun in the genitive by ﴿على﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادر﴾.
﴿الموتى﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿لا﴾: negating, or connective (ṣila) to strengthen the oath.
﴿أقسم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ); and the fāʿil (agent), its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿بيوم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾; and يوم is muḍāf.
﴿القيامة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿ولا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لا is negating, or connective (ṣila) to strengthen the oath.
﴿أقسم﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "I" (أنا).
﴿بالنفس﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أقسم﴾.
﴿اللوامة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿النفس﴾; and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause; and the response to the oath is omitted, i.e.: "you will surely be resurrected", indicated by what comes after it.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿أيحسب﴾: the hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and rebuke (istifhām inkārī tawbīkhī), and يحسب is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative.
﴿ألن﴾: أن is lightened from the heavy (form) (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its ism being the omitted pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn); and لن is a particle of negation, subjunctive and future.
﴿نجمع﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), its fāʿil latent (mustatir), its implied form being "we" (نحن); and the clause ﴿لن نجمع عظامه﴾ is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أن.
﴿عظامه﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the lightened أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of يحسب; and the interrogative clause ﴿أيحسب...﴾ is an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿بلى﴾: a particle of answer, to cancel the negation in ﴿لن نجمع عظامه﴾, i.e.: "yes indeed, We will gather them".
﴿قادرين﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of the implied verb indicated by the particle of answer, i.e.: "yes indeed, We will gather them, being able".
﴿على﴾: a preposition.
﴿أن﴾: a maṣdar-forming and subjunctive particle.
﴿نسوي﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), its fāʿil a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being: "we" (نحن); the maṣdar-forming أن with what falls within its scope is construed as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that is genitive by ﴿على﴾, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿قادرين﴾.
﴿بنانه﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿بل﴾: for transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿يريد﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative.
﴿ليفجر﴾: the lām is causal (taʿlīl), and يفجر: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the causal lām; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir), its implied form being ﴿هو﴾, referring to الإنسان; the interpreted maṣdar from the implied ﴿أن﴾ and the imperfect verb is genitive by the causal lām; the lām with its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يريد﴾; and the object of يريد is omitted, indicated by the cause given in the saying of the Exalted ﴿ليفجر أمامه﴾, its implied form being: "man wants his lusts and his sins". Or the lām in ﴿ليفجر﴾ is connective (ṣila), and يفجر is an imperfect verb, subjunctive by an implied أن after the lām, and the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يفجر﴾ is the object of يريد, its implied form being: "man wants wickedness".
﴿أمامه﴾: أمام is an adverb, accusative; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and the clause ﴿يريد...﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause ﴿أيحسب﴾, or resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿يسأل﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿أيان﴾: an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of time; it is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿يوم﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); and it is muḍāf.
﴿القيامة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). And the clause is in the place of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil of يريد or from the fāʿil of يفجر; or it is resumptive, expressing wonder at their state in asking about the time of the Day of Resurrection — it being a question of mockery, since they believe it impossible that it will happen — and so has no grammatical position; or it is a badal (substitute) of the clause ﴿يريد﴾, and so has no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إذا is an adverb for future time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the response, which is: يقول.
﴿برق﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿البصر﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause ﴿برق البصر﴾ is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it; and the clause is resumptive with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿وخسف﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿القمر﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وجمع﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa.
﴿الشمس﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿والقمر﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and القمر is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to الشمس, nominative.

muyesser-irab:10-10.t:
﴿يقول﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿الإنسان﴾: fāʿil (agent), nominative; and the clause يقول الإنسان has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition.
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿يقول﴾; and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for a clause, the implied form being: "man will say on the day when the sight is dazzled, and the moon is eclipsed, and the sun and the moon are joined together".
﴿أين﴾: أين is an interrogative noun in the position of the accusative as an adverb of place; the adverb is attached to an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate).
﴿المفر﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:11-11.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لا﴾: the lā of generic negation (lā al-nāfiya li-l-jins).
﴿وزر﴾: the ism (noun) of lā, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa; its khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: "existing, available to them".

muyesser-irab:12-12.t:
﴿إلى ربك﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted, fronted khabar (predicate); رب is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, attached to the omitted khabar to which the preposition and its genitive noun are attached; and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi; the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when the sight is dazzled … etc."
﴿المستقر﴾: postponed mubtadaʾ (subject).

muyesser-irab:13-13.t:
﴿ينبأ﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is not named (passive).
﴿الإنسان﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), nominative (marfūʿ). And the clause ﴿ينبأ الإنسان﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ينبأ﴾; and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when the sight is dazzled … etc."
﴿بما﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
﴿قدم﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو). And the clause ﴿قَدَّم﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of ﴿ما﴾, with no grammatical position.
﴿وأخر﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, its fāʿil latent, its implied form being: "he" (هو). And the clause ﴿أخر﴾ is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila clause ﴿قدم﴾, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:14-14.t:
﴿بل﴾: a conjunction and (particle of) transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿الإنسان﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿على نفسه﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿بصيرة﴾; نفس is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿بصيرة﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative.

muyesser-irab:15-15.t:
﴿ولو﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), (the clause being a ḥāl) from the agent concealed in ﴿بصيرة﴾; and لو is conditional.
﴿ألقى﴾: a past verb, and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "he" (هو).
﴿معاذيره﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, i.e.: "they would not be acceptable, and would not be accepted".

muyesser-irab:16-16.t:
﴿لا﴾: prohibitive (nāhiya).
﴿تحرك﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by ﴿لا﴾.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تحرك﴾.
﴿لسانك﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); لسان is muḍāf, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿لتعجل﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (lām al-taʿlīl), and تعجل is an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb) by an implied أن after the lām of cause; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and the verb is genitive by the lām; and the lām with its genitive noun are attached to ﴿تحرك﴾.
﴿به﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تعجل﴾; and the pronoun in ﴿به﴾ refers to the Qur'an.

muyesser-irab:17-17.t:
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿علينا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿جمعه﴾: the postponed ism (noun) of inna.
﴿وقرآنه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and قرآنه is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to جمعه; قرآن is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:18-18.t:
﴿فإذا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and إذا is an adverb for future time.
﴿قرأناه﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn because it is attached to the ﴿نا﴾ of the agents; the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the clause قرأناه is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿فاتبع﴾: the fāʾ binds the response of ﴿إذا﴾, and اتبع is an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "you" (أنت).
﴿قرآنه﴾: قرآن is mafʿūl bihi; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:19-19.t:
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay (tarākhī).
﴿إن﴾: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh).
﴿علينا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the fronted khabar (predicate) of inna.
﴿بيانه﴾: بيان is the postponed ism (noun) of inna; it is muḍāf, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

muyesser-irab:20-20.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿بل﴾: a particle of transitional digression (iḍrāb intiqālī).
﴿تحبون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent).
﴿العاجلة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:21-21.t:
﴿وتذرون﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding clause.
﴿الآخرة﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

muyesser-irab:22-22.t:
﴿وجوه﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ).
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ناضرة﴾; and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when the Resurrection takes place".
﴿ناضرة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وجوه﴾, or a first khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:23-23.t:
﴿إلى ربها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿ناظرة﴾.
﴿ناظرة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of وجوه.

muyesser-irab:24-24.t:
﴿ووجوه﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and وجوه is mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative (marfūʿ); and the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what preceded.
﴿يومئذ﴾: يوم: an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿باسرة﴾; and إذٍ: a noun indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) sukūn, because its place is occupied by the tanwīn of compensation, in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the tanwīn compensates for an omitted clause, the implied form being: "on the day when the Resurrection takes place".
﴿باسرة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿وجوه﴾, or a first khabar (predicate).

muyesser-irab:25-25.t:
﴿تظن﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "they" (هي); and the clause is the khabar (predicate) of وجوه.
﴿أن﴾: maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
﴿يفعل﴾: an imperfect verb, subjunctive (manṣūb), and it is built for an unnamed agent (passive); and أن with what falls within its scope stands in place of the two objects of ﴿تظن﴾.
﴿بها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿يفعل﴾.
﴿فاقرة﴾: nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).

muyesser-irab:26-26.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿إذا﴾: an adverb for future time.
﴿بلغت﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is for the feminine; the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being: "it" (هي); and the clause بلغت is in the position of the genitive by the adverb being put in annexation to it.
﴿التراقي﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
So most of the readers read it. It is reported from al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj: «لأقسم بيوم القيامة», taking it as the lām of the oath, with no alif in it. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a solecism according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh; one only says [it] with the nūn:
لأقومن. As for the first reading, there are several views on it. Among them is that «لا» is redundant (zāʾida), for emphasis, like ما مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ [al-Aʿrāf: 12]. In al-Farrāʾ's view this is wrong on two counts: first, that when «لا» is redundant one does not begin [speech] with it; and second, that «لا» is only added in a negative context, as [the poet] said: [al-Basīṭ] 511-
ما كان يرضى رسول الله فعلهما ... والطيّبان أبو بكر ولا عمر
(The Messenger of Allah would not have approved their deed, nor the two good men, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.)
i.e. Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, with «لا» redundant. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for his statement that «لا» is not added at the beginning of speech, it is as he said — there is no disagreement about it, because that would be confusing. But he has been opposed in what he said: as I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say, this view is sound — meaning the view of whoever said that «لا» is redundant. He said:
His statement that it is at the beginning of the speech does not refute this view, because the whole Quran has the status of a single sūra, and on this basis is its arrangement, composition and structure. It is soundly reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down the Quran all at once to the lowest heaven in the month of Ramaḍān, and then it came down piecemeal from heaven; and only the people of innovation reject this ḥadīth. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for al-Farrāʾ's statement that «لا» is only added in a negative context, he is contradicted on it. This was reported by those among the Basrans whose knowledge is trusted, among them Abū ʿUbayda, who recited: [al-Rajaz] 512- في بئر لا حور سرى وما شعر (He travelled by night into a well of perdition, and he did not perceive it.) He said: he means في بئر حور, i.e. [a well of] destruction; so he added «لا» in an affirmative context. Al-Farrāʾ disagreed with him on this and made «لا» a negation here, i.e. "in a well that yields nothing back". Al-Farrāʾ claimed that the «لا» in His saying «لا أقسم» is a rejection of their words, as you say: لا والله ما أفعل ("No! By Allah, I will not do it"); so the pause is at it [i.e. at لا], and أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ (1) is a new beginning (mustaʾnaf).

nahhas-irab:2-2.t: There is no disagreement in this [verse] that the alif comes after «لا». So the view of al-Ḥasan is that «لا» is negating; and we have explained the views of others.

nahhas-irab:3-3.t: The reading of the Kufans is أَيَحْسَبُ; and the past is حسب, without disagreement, so the regular form in the imperfect is يحسب [with fatḥa], except that kasra has been reported from the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-irab:4-4.t:
قادِرِينَ is in the position of naṣb (accusative), and there are several views on its accusative. Among them: it has been said that the construction is "Yes, We are able (نقدر)", and when نقدر was converted to قادرين it was put in the accusative, as al-Farazdaq said: [al-Ṭawīl] 513-
على حلفة لا أشتم الدّهر مسلما ... ولا خارجا من فيّ زور كلام
(By an oath that I will never revile a Muslim, nor will false speech go out from my mouth.)
in the sense of ولا يخرج; and when يخرج was converted to خارج it was put in the accusative. This is wrong, because each has its own inflection: you say جاءني زيد يضحك and جاءني زيد ضاحكا, and مررت برجل يضحك and برجل ضاحك. «ولا خارجا» is conjoined to the position of «لا أشتم». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the soundest thing said about it. And it has been said that the construction is: "Yes, We are capable of that, being able (قادرين)" — this is the view of al-Farrāʾ. Sībawayh said: i.e. "Yes, We will gather them, being able". Al-Farrāʾ's view is derived from this. And بنان is the plural of بنانة. Among the good things said about it is the statement of Ibn ʿAbbās: "We are able to make his fingertips a single thing, like the hoof of a camel or the hoof of a donkey, so that he would not be able to eat with them [and would eat] like the beasts; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, was bounteous to him and favoured him." And al-Ḥasan said: "We were able to make his fingers of one size, so that they would have no beauty and he could hardly benefit from them."

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: This is the lām of kay (purpose); and their calling it the lām of «إنّ» has no meaning. Rather, يريد indicates intention, i.e. his intention is to act wickedly in what lies ahead of him.

nahhas-irab:6-6.t: The construction is: "at what time is the Day of Resurrection?" And the nūn of إيان «[Translator's note: so in the source, for أيّان.]» has fatḥa because of the meeting of two vowelless letters.

nahhas-irab:7-8.t: فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ (7) is the reading of Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim, Shayba, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; and Naṣr ibn ʿĀṣim, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, Abū Jaʿfar and Nāfiʿ read فَإِذا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ with fatḥa on the rāʾ «[Translator's note: the source prints the same vowels for both readings; the second is بَرَقَ.]». The meaning of the kasra is clear, i.e. it is bewildered and terrified by death and by the matter of the Resurrection; and برق [means] it flashed and gleamed. Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ (8): its light went away.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: It may be said: الشّمس is feminine without disagreement, so why did He not say وجمعت? There are several answers to this. Among them is that the construction is "and [it was] gathered between the sun and the moon", so the masculine was construed with بين. And it has been said: since "and the sun was gathered" does not complete the sentence until one says "and the moon", and the moon is masculine, the meaning was plural, so their verb had to be masculine when placed first, as it would be when placed after. The most appropriate thing said about it is the view of al-Kisāʾī; he said: the meaning is "and the two lights, i.e. the two luminaries, were gathered"; and in another place: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الشَّمْسَ بازِغَةً قالَ هذا رَبِّي [al-Anʿām: 78]. As for Muḥammad ibn Yazīd, he says: all this is a non-real feminine, because it was not made feminine to distinguish between one thing and another, so you may treat it as masculine, since it has the meaning of "a body" and "a thing".

nahhas-irab:10-10.t:
This is a maṣdar (verbal noun) without disagreement, i.e. "where is the fleeing?" Ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said:
I heard Ibn ʿAbbās read أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ «[Translator's note: the source prints the standard vowels; Ibn ʿAbbās's reading is الْمَفِرُّ, with kasra.]». Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a sound chain of transmission; and in the view of the Basrans it is a noun of place. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that he permits kasra in the maṣdar.

nahhas-irab:11-11.t: And it [الوزر] is the place of refuge. It has been said: وزير (minister) is derived from this, because the one he serves has handed his affairs over to him, so he resorts to him and relies on him. And it has been said: because the burdens (أوزار) of what the one he serves takes on are in his hand; and أوزار [also] means what consists of gold, silver and other things.

nahhas-irab:12-12.t: Qatāda said: [الْمُسْتَقَرُّ means] the final end.

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Among the best of what has been said about it is the statement of Qatāda; he said: of what he sent forward of obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and what he held back of His due — he will be informed of all of it. Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: of what he sent forward of good or evil after him «[Translator's note: so in the source; presumably "what he sent forward, and what he left behind after him".]».

nahhas-irab:14-14.t:
It is difficult in its i'rab and its meaning. The view of Ibn ʿAbbās is: his hearing, his sight, his hands, his feet and his limbs are witnesses against him. Abū Jaʿfar said: according to this view, الْإِنْسانُ
is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and بَصِيرَةٌ
is a second mubtadaʾ, and «على نفسه» is the khabar (predicate) of the second, and the clause is the khabar of the first. Its explanation is: "rather, man has, over himself, from himself, watchers that keep record of him and testify against him." That is one view. The view of Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and Qatāda is that the man is himself the بصيرة (witness). Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: man, by Allah, is a witness against himself. Qatāda said: you see him, by Allah, aware of others' sins and faults, heedless of himself. According to this view «الإنسان» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ and «بصيرة» is its khabar. If it is asked: why was the hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] added when الإنسان is masculine? There are two answers to this. One of them is that the hāʾ is for intensiveness, as one says رجل راوية and علّامة. And it has been said: the hāʾ was added because the meaning is "rather, man is a proof (حجّة) against himself".

nahhas-irab:15-15.t: [مَعاذِيرَهُ is] a plural not according to rule in the view of Sībawayh, because the plural of عذر is not معاذير; معاذير is rather the plural of معذار.

nahhas-irab:16-17.t:
إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ
(17): so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, guarantees its collection. For this reason the jurists declared an unbeliever whoever claims that something of it has remained [uncollected], because that is a rejection of the plain text of the revelation. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna was asked: how were the Torah and the Gospel altered, when they are both from Allah? He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, entrusted their preservation to them — He, exalted be His praise, said: بِمَا اسْتُحْفِظُوا مِنْ كِتابِ اللَّهِ [al-Māʾida: 44] — but He did not entrust the preservation of the Quran to anyone; He said: إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّكْرَ وَإِنَّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ [al-Ḥijr: 9]; and what He preserves is not altered.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t:
The scholars differed about the meaning of this. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "So when We send it down, listen to it." Qatāda said: i.e. follow what it makes lawful and unlawful. Among the good things said about it is what Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ
— he said: He says: "So when We have made it clear" — فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ
— he said:
He says: "Then act according to what is in it."

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: Qatāda said: [it means] making clear the lawful as distinct from the unlawful. From Ibn ʿAbbās: بَيانَهُ "on your tongue".

nahhas-irab:20-20.t: I.e. the immediate state, or the immediate world.

nahhas-irab:21-21.t: Because it [الْآخِرَةَ] comes after the first [world].

nahhas-irab:24-24.t: [وُجُوهٌ ... باسِرَةٌ is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: It is not permissible to put يفعل [i.e. يُفْعَلَ] in the nominative, while it was permissible in وَحَسِبُوا أَلَّا تَكُونَ فِتْنَةٌ [al-Māʾida: 71], because «لا» is a compensation [for the omitted pronoun]. And الفاقرة means the calamity, the enormous matter.

nahhas-irab:26-27.t:
كَلَّا may mean "truly" (حقا), and on this basis it would here be a beginning (mubtadaʾ) [of speech] «[Translator's note: i.e. one begins with it rather than pausing before it.]». Muḥammad ibn Jarīr claimed that the full stop here is at «كلا», and that the meaning is: the matter is not as the polytheists say, that they will not be requited for their polytheism and disobedience. إِذا بَلَغَتِ التَّراقِيَ: the governing word of إذا may be «باسرة» or «بلغت»; if the governing word is «بلغت», the apodosis is in what follows. The yāʾ was dropped from مَنْ راقٍ
because it is vowelless and the tanwīn is vowelless, and it was kept in التراقي because there is no tanwīn in it.

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: [It is] in the position of the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t:
فَلا صَدَّقَ وَلا صَلَّى: لا here is a negation and not a conjunction. According to the grammarians it is not permissible to say:
ضربت زيدا لا ضربت عمرا; the reason for this is that it was disliked for the second to resemble an imprecation. In the verse, the meaning is "he did not believe and did not pray"; what indicates this is وَلكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّى.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t: I.e. he went off turning away from obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, disdaining the admonition; and يَتَمَطَّى is in the position of naṣb (accusative) as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

nahhas-irab:34-35.t: [أَوْلى لَكَ] is said to someone who has fallen into destruction or come close to it.

nahhas-irab:36-36.t: [سُدىً is] likewise in the position of naṣb (accusative) as a ḥāl (circumstantial). Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the meaning of «أن يترك سدّى» is — he says — "neglected".

nahhas-irab:37-37.t: [يُمْنى with yāʾ is] according to the masculine of المني, which is closer to it; and «تمنى» [with tāʾ] refers to the نطفة.

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: I.e. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, created him and fashioned him into a human being who speaks, hears and sees.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: It has been said: the meaning is "and He made of man offspring, males and females". الذكر والأنثى are a badal (substitute) from الزوجين.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t: So He, Mighty and Majestic, gave a clear indication that His bringing him back to life after death is no greater than His creating him from a drop of fluid and then fashioning him into a human being until children were born to him. Al-Farrāʾ permitted عَلى أَنْ يُحْيِيَ الْمَوْتى «[Translator's note: i.e. as يُحْيِّ.]» by transferring the vowel of the first yāʾ to the ḥāʾ and assimilating the yāʾ into the yāʾ. This is wrong according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh. The reason for this — and it is the sense of what Abū Isḥāq said — is that when you say «يحيي», assimilation is not permissible by consensus of the grammarians, so that two vowelless letters do not meet; and when you say أن يحيي, assimilation is also not permissible, because the yāʾ, even though it has taken a vowel, its vowel is accidental. Moreover, how could a single letter be assimilated in a position because of a governing word that has entered upon it and is not permanent, while it may not be assimilated when it is in the position of rafʿ (nominative) — and the nominative is the basic state?

nahhas-irab:22-23.t:
وُجُوهٌ is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); ناضِرَةٌ is a naʿt (adjective) of it, and ناظِرَةٌ is the khabar (predicate) of the subject. «ناضرة» may [also] be the khabar of «وجوه» and ناظِرَةٌ a second khabar; and ناضرة may be a naʿt of ناظرة or of وجوه. One also says أجوه; and it [وجوه] is the plural for many, while for few it is أوجه. On ناظِرَةٌ there are three views: one is that the meaning is "waiting"; another is that the meaning is "[looking] to the reward of its Lord"; and another is that they look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
He said: the correct one among these answers is known from the Arabic language; for that reason and others we postponed its explanation in order to mention it in the i'rab. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the view of whoever said that its meaning is "waiting", it is wrong. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: نظرت إليه [with إلى] does not mean "I waited for him"; one only says نظرته [for that]. This is the view of Ibrāhīm ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿArafa and others whose knowledge is trusted. As for whoever said that the meaning is "to the reward of its Lord", it is also wrong according to the view of the leading grammarians, because in their view — and in the view of anyone I know — نظرت زيدا is not permissible in the sense of "I looked at his reward". We will mention the argumentation on this from the words of the imams, the scholars and the lexicographers, since it is one of the foundations of the Sunna, and we will mention what the people of whims opposed it with. We begin with the sound ḥadīths from the Messenger ﷺ, since he is the one who makes clear [what comes] from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As was read before Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb ibn ʿAlī, from Isḥāq ibn Rāhawayh: Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd narrated to us: Baḥīr ibn Saʿd narrated to us, from Khālid ibn Maʿdān, from ʿAmr ibn al-Aswad, that Qatāda ibn Abī Umayya narrated to them from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: "I have told you about the Masīḥ al-Dajjāl until I feared that you would not understand. He is short, bow-legged, curly-haired, one-eyed, his left eye effaced, neither protruding nor sunken. If you are confused about him, then know that your Lord is not one-eyed. You will not see your Lord, exalted be His praise, until you die." Aḥmad ibn Shuʿayb said: Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us; he said: Abū ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays al-Ashʿarī, from his father, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Two gardens of silver — their vessels and all that is in them; and two gardens of gold — their vessels and all that is in them; and nothing stands between the people and their looking at their Lord, exalted be His praise, except the cloak of grandeur over His face, in the Garden of ʿAdn." And it was read before Abū al-Qāsim ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad al-Baghawī, from Hudba ibn Khālid, from Ḥammād ibn Salama, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Laylā «[Translator's note: so in the source; in the known chain, Ḥammād narrates from Thābit al-Bunānī from Ibn Abī Laylā.]», from Ṣuhayb, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this verse: لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا الْحُسْنى وَزِيادَةٌ [Yūnus: 26] and said: "When the people of the Garden enter the Garden and the people of the Fire enter the Fire, a caller calls out: 'O people of the Garden, you have an appointment with Allah which He wishes to fulfil for you.' They say: 'What is it? Has He not made our scales heavy, whitened our faces, admitted us into the Garden and saved us from the Fire?' Then the veil is lifted for them, and they look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic; and nothing they have been given is dearer to them than looking at Him — and that is the 'more' (al-ziyāda)." Abū al-Qāsim said: and my grandfather narrated to me; he said: Yazīd ibn Hārūn narrated to us from Ḥammād ibn Salama, with his chain, the like of it. Abū al-Qāsim said: and Hārūn ibn ʿAbd Allāh narrated to me; he said: I heard Yazīd — meaning Ibn Hārūn — when he narrated this ḥadīth, say: whoever denies this ḥadīth is a zindīq or an unbeliever. Abū al-Qāsim said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Kūfī narrated to us, from Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī al-Juʿfī, from Zāʾida: Bayān al-Bajalī narrated to us, from Qays ibn Abī Ḥāzim, who said: Jarīr narrated to us; he said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out to us and said:
"You will see your Lord on the Day of Resurrection as you see this; you will not be crowded together (لا تضامون) in seeing Him" — meaning the moon. Ḥusayn al-Juʿfī said: in spite of Jahm «[Translator's note: the source has «جهيم».]» and al-Marīsī. Abū al-Qāsim said: Aḥmad ibn Ibrāhīm al-ʿAbdī and Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us; they said: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Idrīs narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, who said: we said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we see our Lord, exalted be His praise?" He said:
"Do you harm one another (أتضارون) in seeing the sun at midday when there is no cloud?" We said: "No." He said: "Do you harm one another in seeing the moon on the night it is full when there is no cloud?" We said: "No." He said: "Then you will not harm one another in seeing Him, just as you do not harm one another in seeing them." Abū al-Qāsim said: and I was told from Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, from Yaḥyā ibn Ādam, from Abū Bakr ibn ʿAyyāsh, who said: al-Aʿmash said: لا تضارّون means "you will not dispute with one another". Abū al-Qāsim said: and Hudba ibn Khālid narrated to us: Wuhayb ibn Khālid narrated to us: Muṣʿab ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Abū Ṣāliḥ al-Sammān, from Abū Hurayra, who said: it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, will every one of us see his Lord, exalted be His mention, on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Does every one of you see the sun at midday when there is no cloud in the sky?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Does every one of you see the moon on the night it is full when there is no cloud in the sky?" They said: "Yes." He said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will see your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection; you will not harm one another in seeing Him, just as you do not harm one another in seeing them." Abū al-Qāsim said: ʿUthmān ibn Abī Shayba narrated to us: Abū Usāma narrated to us: al-Aʿmash narrated to us: Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān informed me, from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī, who said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is none of you but his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, will speak to him, with no interpreter between Him and him, and no veil screening him. He will look to his right and see nothing but what he sent forward; then he will look to his left and see nothing but what he sent forward; then he will look in front of him and see nothing but the Fire. So guard yourselves against the Fire, even with half a date." In this ḥadīth from al-Aʿmash, no one said "and no veil screening him" except Abū Usāma alone. And of that is what Aḥmad ibn ʿAlī ibn Suhayl narrated to us: Zuhayr — meaning Ibn Ḥarb — narrated to us: Ismāʿīl narrated to us, from Hishām al-Dastawāʾī, from Qatāda, from Ṣafwān ibn Muḥriz, who said:
A man said to Ibn ʿUmar: "How did you hear the Messenger of Allah ﷺ speak about the private conversation (al-najwā)?" He said: I heard him say: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection, until He places His cover over him and makes him confess his sins, saying: 'Do you recognise [them]?' He says: 'My Lord, I recognise [them].' He says: 'I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today.' Then he will be given the record of his reckoning. As for the unbelievers and the hypocrites, they will be proclaimed before the heads of all creatures: 'These are the ones who lied against Allah.'" Abū Jaʿfar said: on this subject there are [ḥadīths] from Anas and from Abū Razīn from the Prophet ﷺ, and on it there are [reports] from the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them — among them Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq and Ḥudhayfa — [and] from the Followers; but we disliked lengthiness, since the ḥadīth we have mentioned suffices. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Aḥmad ibn ʿAbd al-Salām narrated to us: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā al-Naysābūrī say:
The Sunna in our view — and it is the view of our imams Mālik ibn Anas, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿUmar «[Translator's note: so in the source; the name appears corrupt.]», al-Awzāʿī, Sufyān ibn Saʿīd al-Thawrī, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna al-Hilālī and Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and the people of knowledge whom we have known have held it — is that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will be seen in the Hereafter with the eyes: the people of the Garden will see Him, but as for the rest of the children of Adam, they will not. He said: the proof for this is the ḥadīths transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ, that it was said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, will we see our Lord on the Day of Resurrection?" — and he mentioned the ḥadīth. Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā said: and belief in these ḥadīths transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — on seeing the Lord at the Resurrection; on the decree; intercession; the punishment of the grave; the Basin; the Balance; the Dajjāl; stoning; the descent of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, every night after the half or the remaining third; the reckoning; the Fire and the Garden — that both are created and do not pass away; and that there is no one but Allah will speak to him on the Day of Resurrection with no interpreter between Him and him to interpret for him; and similar ḥadīths — and affirming them is binding upon the servants: they must believe in them, even if their minds do not reach them and they do not know their explanation. They must believe in them and submit, without [asking] how, without aversion «[Translator's note: «تنفير» in the source; perhaps «تفسير», "interpretation".]» and without analogy, because the acts of Allah are not likened to the acts of the servants.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the speech of the scholars known for [adherence to] the Sunna in every age, until it reached Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn Jarīr. He mentioned the words of those who deny the vision, their argumentation and their sophistry, refuted that and made it clear; and we will mention his words verbatim, since he achieved in it what was intended, if Allah wills. He mentioned their objection from His saying, Exalted is He: لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ وَهُوَ يُدْرِكُ الْأَبْصارَ [al-Anʿām: 103]. As for His saying, Mighty and Majestic: قالَ رَبِّ أَرِنِي أَنْظُرْ إِلَيْكَ قالَ لَنْ تَرانِي [al-Aʿrāf: 143], it is something that needs no argument, because it contains evidence for the looking: since Mūsā ﷺ, with his rank, could not ask for what cannot be, this shows that it is possible for it to be; and the time at which he asked it was in this world, so the answer is that no one sees Him in this world. And he argued against their sophistry concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, لا تدركه الأبصار, with the statement of ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ ناضِرَةٌ إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ — he said: they will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic; their sight will not encompass Him because of His greatness, while His sight encompasses them; and that is His saying: لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ. He said: those who hold this view argued from His saying, Mighty and Majestic: حَتَّى إِذا أَدْرَكَهُ الْغَرَقُ [Yūnus: 90] — and drowning is not described as having seen him. They said: so the meaning of «لا تدركه الأبصار» is far from the meaning of "they do not see Him", because a thing may overtake (يدرك) a thing without seeing it, as in «حتّى إذا أدركه الغرق»; and likewise a thing may see a thing without overtaking it. Similar is: قالَ أَصْحابُ مُوسى إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 61] — Pharaoh's people had seen them but had not overtaken them. And He, exalted be His praise, said: لا تَخافُ دَرَكاً [Ṭā Hā: 77]. So since a thing may see a thing without overtaking it, and overtake it without seeing it, it is known that «لا تدركه الأبصار» is far removed from the meaning "eyes do not see Him", and that its meaning is "eyes do not encompass Him", because encompassing Him is not possible. The believers and the people of the Garden will see their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, yet their eyes will not "overtake" Him, in the sense that they will not encompass Him, since it is not permissible to describe Allah as being encompassed by anything. Parallel to the permissibility of describing Him as being seen but not encompassed is the permissibility of describing Him as being known but not encompassed. He, Blessed and Exalted, said: وَلا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِما شاءَ [al-Baqara: 255]; the meaning of العلم here is "what is known". So His denying that His creatures encompass anything of His knowledge, except what He wills, was not a denial that they know it; it is only a denial of encompassing it. Likewise, in denying that sight overtakes Allah, Mighty and Majestic, when it sees Him, there is no denial of its seeing Him. Just as it is possible for creatures to know something without encompassing it in knowledge, so it is possible for them to see their Lord with their eyes without their eyes "overtaking" Him, since the meaning of seeing is other than the meaning of overtaking, and the meaning of overtaking is other than the meaning of seeing, because the meaning of overtaking is encompassing, as Ibn ʿAbbās said: eyes do not encompass Him, and He encompasses them. If it is said: "And why do you reject that the meaning of «لا تدركه الأبصار» is 'they do not see Him'?" we say to him: we reject that because Allah informed in His Book that faces at the Resurrection will be looking at Allah, glory be to Him, and the Prophet ﷺ informed that they will see their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Resurrection as they see the moon on the night it is full and as they see the sun with no cloud before it. The Book of Allah confirms itself, part by part; so it is known that the meaning of لا تُدْرِكُهُ الْأَبْصارُ is other than the meaning of إِلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ. He said: and it has been said: the meaning is that the eyes of creatures do not perceive Him in this world but will perceive Him in the Hereafter — so they made this specific. He said: and it has been said:
The meaning is that the eyes of the wrongdoers do not perceive Him in this world or the Hereafter, while the eyes of the believers perceive Him. And it has been said: «لا تدركه الأبصار» [means] by reaching the limit and encompassing; as for seeing — yes. And it has been said: eyes do not perceive Him as He perceives creatures, because their eyes are weak. Others said: the verse is general, and the sight of no one will ever perceive Allah, exalted be His praise, in this world or the Hereafter; but Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will create for His friends on the Day of Resurrection a sixth sense besides their five senses, and they will see Him with it. The correct view on this, in our opinion, is what the reports from the Prophet ﷺ concur on: "You will see your Lord" — so the believers will see Him, and the unbelievers on that day will be veiled. The people of this doctrine have things with which they cause confusion: some of them reject the ḥadīth out of obstinacy and to attack the people of Islam, and some of them bring things that we dislike to mention. Muḥammad ibn Jarīr said: we have only mentioned this so that whoever looks into what we mean «[Translator's note: «نعني» in the source; perhaps «في كتابنا».]» may know that they fall back in their doctrine only on what Satan has confused for them, whose corruption the people of truth can easily expose; they do not fall back in their doctrine on any verse of the revelation, nor on any report from the Messenger, sound or weak. So they stumble about in darkness and wander in blindness. We seek refuge with Allah from bewilderment and misguidance. Abū Jaʿfar said: as for the explanation of «تضارون» and the variation in its transmission, we will dictate it. There are eight forms in it: it is transmitted «تضارون» with a light [rāʾ] and «تضامون» with a light [mīm]; and تضامّون and تضارّون «[Translator's note: the source repeats «تضامّون» twice here; the second is evidently تضارّون.]» are permissible with ḍamma on the tāʾ and a doubled mīm and rāʾ; and تضامّون is permissible on the basis that the original is تتضامّون, with a tāʾ dropped, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: وَلا تَفَرَّقُوا [Āl ʿImrān: 103]; and تضّامّون is permissible, assimilating the tāʾ into the ḍād; and تضارّون is permissible, with the tāʾ dropped; and تضّارّون is permissible, assimilating the tāʾ into the ḍād. What the meticulous transmitters have related is the light form: تضامون and تضارون. I heard Abū Isḥāq say: its meaning is "no injustice (ضيم) and no harm (ضير) will befall you in seeing Him", i.e. you will see Him so that you are all equal in seeing, and none of you will wrong another, nor will any of you harm another. The lexicographers gave two other views. They said: لا تضارّون with a doubled rāʾ and لا تضامّون with a doubled mīm, with ḍamma on the tāʾ; and some of them said: with fatḥa on the tāʾ and a doubled rāʾ and mīm, in the sense of تتضامّون and تتضارّون. The meaning of this is that none of you will contend with another, i.e. none of you will disagree with another in that. One says ضاررت فلانا أضارّه مضارّة وضرارا, when you disagree with him. And the meaning of لا تضامّون في رؤيته is that none of you will press up to another, one saying to the other "Show Him to me", as they do when looking for the new moon.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what we mentioned of al-Aʿmash's explanation, that its meaning is لا تضارّون [you will not dispute], requires that his transmission be لا تضارّون, the original being لا تضاررون «[Translator's note: the source has «لا تضارون»; the unassimilated form تضاررون is evidently meant.]», with the rāʾ then assimilated into the rāʾ. And whoever says its meaning is لا تضارّون, the original in his view is لا تضارون «[Translator's note: again, تضاررون is evidently meant.]», then assimilated. All of this is from ضارّه, when he disagrees with him, as Abū Isḥāq reported — "he disagreed with him and the two did not share one view" «[Translator's note: the source has «وخالفه وما رآه واحد», which seems corrupt; translated tentatively.]». And one says: نضر وجهه, نضرا, نضارة and نضرة; and نضره الله ينضره and أنضره ينضره, from radiance, bliss, a good life and wealth.

safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) redundant (zāʾida) [Note: It was said that (لا) is not redundant but is for negation, and there are two explanations of that: the first, that it negates swearing by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul; the second, that it is a rejection of implied speech, as though they had said "You are fabricating against Allah concerning the resurrection", so He said "No", then began with the oath.. And it has parallels in the speech of the Arabs.]; (بيوم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسم), and likewise (لا أقسم بالنفس ...).
The clause «أقسم ...» has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أقسم (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the opening clause.. And the answer of the oath for both clauses is omitted, indicated by what follows it, i.e. لتبعثنّ "you will surely be raised".
3- (الهمزة) for interrogation of reproach and rebuke; (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted [Note: Its noun may be the first-person plural pronoun of majesty, i.e. أنّنا لن نجمع ...].
The clause «يحسب الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لن نجمع ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the lightened (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن نجمع ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسب.
4- (بلى) an answering particle affirming a negated question, i.e. "yes, We shall gather them"; (قادرين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil (agent) of the implied verb; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نسوّي ...) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (قادرين).
The clause «(نجمعها) قادرين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نسوّي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(اللوّامة): feminine of اللوّام, an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from the triliteral لام; its pattern is فعّال, and the feminine is فعّالة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The art of sound division, or harmony between meanings: the saying of Allah the Exalted «لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ وَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ».
This verse is counted among the beauties of division, because of the harmony of the two things sworn by: He first swore by the Day of Resurrection, then swore by the souls that are requited in it, upon the reality of the resurrection and the requital.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (اللام) redundant (zāʾida); (يفجر) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (أمامه) an adverb borrowed for time — it was for place — accusative [Note: I.e. man wishes to continue in his wickedness in the time that lies ahead of him.]; (أيّان) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (يوم).
The clause «يريد الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يفجر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفجر ...) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يريد — and this is the remote position —. The clause «يسأل ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يفجر [Note: It may be an explanatory resumption.. or a badal (substitute) of the clause يريد.].
The clause «أيّان يوم ...» is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb يسأل, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, with a preposition implied.

* Morphology:
(5) أمامه: an adverbial noun of place — borrowed in the verse for time —; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(6) أيّان: an interrogative noun — and it may be conditional — used to indicate time; its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:7-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقول), and إذ is an adverbial noun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (أين) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المفرّ).
The clause «برق البصر ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «خسف القمر ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause برق البصر.
The clause «جمع الشمس ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause برق البصر.
The clause «يقول الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أين المفرّ ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(المفرّ): a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral فرّ [Note: It cannot be a noun of place, because that would have to be on مفعل — with kasra on the ʿayn — since its imperfect is يفرّ..]; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; the vowel of the ʿayn was transferred to the letter before it to suit the doubling.

safi-cedvel:11-13.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke against seeking flight; (لا) the lā of generic negation, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being موجود "existing"; (إلى ربّك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المستقرّ); (يومئذ) an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar [Note: It may not be attached to المستقرّ: if it is a mīmī maṣdar, what it governs cannot precede it, and if it is a noun of place, it has no governing power.], and the second (يومئذ) is attached to (ينبّأ); (بما) attached to (ينبّأ)..
The clause «لا وزر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إلى ربّك.. المستقرّ.» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ينبّأ الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قدّم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أخّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(وزر): a noun meaning refuge or fortress; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for digression (al-iḍrāb); (على نفسه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بصيرة) [Note: Or it is a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ بصيرة, with the omission of the thing described, i.e. "a seeing eye" or "seeing limbs", and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الإنسان.], which is the khabar (predicate), and (التاء) is for intensiveness [Note: As one says "So-and-so is a حجّة (proof)" or "an عبرة (lesson)".. And الإنسان may be interpreted as the limbs.]; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «الإنسان.. بصيرة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ألقى ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in بصيرة..
And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "they would not be accepted from him".

* Morphology:
(ألقى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is ألقي — with a yāʾ at its end —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(معاذير): plural of معذرة, irregularly [Note: See verse (165) of al-Aʿrāf.], and it is a collective noun on the view of al-Zamakhsharī..

safi-cedvel:16-19.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive (majzūm); (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحرّك); (اللام) of reason (al-taʿlīl); (تعجل) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعجل) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (تحرّك).
The second (به) is attached to (تعجل); (علينا) attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (الفاء) conjunction, and the second is linking the apodosis.
The clause «لا تحرّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعجل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ علينا جمعه ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the prohibition.
The clause «قرأناه ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اتّبع ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
19- (ثمّ) a conjunction; (علينا) attached to the khabar of the second إنّ; (بيانه) noun of إنّ, accusative..
The clause «إنّ علينا بيانه» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(قرآنه): maṣdar of the triliteral قرأ, annexed to its object, i.e. "your reciting it"; its pattern is فعلان, with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The Prophet's ﷺ eagerness to memorize the Qur'an: This verse points to the Prophet's ﷺ intense eagerness to memorize the verses of revelation, so that they would not slip away from him.
It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to suffer hardship from the revelation, and he used to move his lips, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent down (لا تحرك به لسانك). So after that, when Jibrīl came to him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would listen, and when Jibrīl departed, the Prophet ﷺ would recite it as he had recited it — and in one narration: as Allah the Exalted had promised him. This is the wording of al-Ḥumaydī. Al-Baghawī narrated it by way of al-Bukhārī, and said in it: When Jibrīl came down to the Prophet ﷺ with revelation, he was among those who moved his tongue and lips, and it was hard on him, and that was noticeable in him, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent down the verse: (لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ). He said: It is upon Us to gather it in your breast and that you recite it; (فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ): when We send it down, then listen; (ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ): it is upon Us to make it clear by your tongue. So when Jibrīl came to him he would lower his head, and when he left he would recite it as Allah the Exalted had promised him. And in one narration: he used to move his lips when it was revealed to him, fearing that it would slip away from him, so it was said to him: (لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ), i.e. We gather it in your breast, and قرآنه, i.e. that you recite it.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) for deterrence; (بل) for digression (al-iḍrāb); (الواو) for conjunction.
The clause «تحبّون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تذرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:22-25.t:
* I'rab:
(وجوه) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified.], qualified by the naʿt (adjective) (ناضرة); (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — annexed to the adverbial noun إذ.. attached to (mutaʿalliq) the naʿt ناضرة; (إلى ربّها) attached to the khabar (predicate) (ناظرة); (الواو) conjunction; (وجوه يومئذ باسرة) is like the first verse; (بها) attached to the passive verb (يفعل); (فاقرة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفعل ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يظنّ.
The clause «وجوه ... إلى ربّها ناظرة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «وجوه.. تظنّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تظنّ ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (وجوه).
The clause «يفعل بها فاقرة» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(22) ناضرة: feminine of ناضر, active participle of the triliteral (نضر), on the pattern فاعل, and it is فاعلة.
(24) باسرة: feminine of باسر, active participle of (بسر), meaning "he frowned"; its pattern is فاعل.
(25) فاقرة: a noun for a calamity.. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "the calamity فقرت the man", i.e. befell him; its pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
- Will the believers see their Lord in the Hereafter?
The scholars of Ahl al-Sunna said: The vision of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is possible, not rationally impossible, and they agreed unanimously that it will occur in the Hereafter, and that the believers, not the disbelievers, will see Allah, Glorified and Exalted, as evidenced by the saying of the Exalted: (كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ). Groups among the Muʿtazila, the Khawārij and the Murjiʾa claimed that none of His creation will see Allah the Exalted, and that seeing Him is rationally impossible; but this claim of theirs does not rest on any evidence from the Book or the Sunna, but is based only on opinion and conjecture. The proofs of the Book and the Sunna, and the consensus of the Companions and of the early generations of the community after them, have combined to affirm the vision of Allah the Exalted. About twenty Companions narrated it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the verses of the Qur'an about it are well known, and the objection of the Muʿtazila has well-known answers in the books of the theologians of Ahl al-Sunna, and this is not the place to mention them. Further, the position of the people of truth is that vision is a faculty that Allah places in His creatures, and it does not require the meeting of rays, nor facing the thing seen, nor anything else.
As for the hadiths:
It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is one who looks at his gardens, his spouses, his bliss and his servants over the distance of a thousand years' journey, and the most honoured of them with Allah is one who looks at His Face morning and evening." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: (وجوه يومئذ ناضرة إلى ربها ناظرة).
And from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon, and said: "You will see your Lord with your own eyes as you see this moon; you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in missing a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: (وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ).
Moreover, other sound hadiths have come on this subject, which there is no room to present in full.

safi-cedvel:26-30.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis indicated by His saying (إلى ربّك يومئذ المساق), and the fāʿil (agent) of (بلغت) is omitted, indicated by the context, namely the spirit or the soul; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (من) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (راق), which is nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (بالساق) attached to (التفّت); (إلى ربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (المساق); (يومئذ) an adverb of time, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — attached to what the adverb إذا is attached to, so it is a badal (substitute) of it..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه الفراق ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّ.
The clause «بلغت ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت.
The clause «من راق ...» is in the position of a nominative: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: It is originally the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).].
The clause «ظنّ ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت..
The clause «التفّت الساق ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت..
The clause «إلى ربّك ... المساق» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis of إذا, i.e.:
"when it reaches the collarbones.. it is driven to the judgment of its Lord".

* Morphology:
(التراقي): plural of ترقوة, a noun for the upper bone that extends from the breastbone to the shoulder, or it is the front of the throat at the top of the chest where the breath rises; its pattern is تفعلة, with fatḥa on the tāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām, and the pattern of التراقي is تفاعل. In it there is a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is التراقو: what preceded the wāw had kasra, so it was turned into a yāʾ.
(راق): active participle of (رقي) or of (رقى): the first meaning "he ascended", of the pattern-class فرح, and the second meaning "he recited over him to cure him", of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فاع. In it there is a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it is defective (manqūṣ).
(المساق): a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral ساق; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. In it there is a weak-letter change by conversion; its original form is مسوق, with fatḥa on the mīm and the wāw and a quiescent letter between them..
The fatḥa of the wāw was transferred to the sīn and the wāw was made quiescent — a weak-letter change by quiescence —; the sīn was vowelled with fatḥa before the wāw, so the wāw was turned into an alif — a weak-letter change by conversion —.

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ».
In the noble verse there is a representational metaphor for the severity of parting from what one is accustomed to — homeland, family, children and friend — and the severity of coming before one's Lord, majestic is His affair. The two severities have become entwined with each other, as the shank is entwined with the shank. And one says "the war bared its shank" as a metaphor for its severity.

safi-cedvel:31-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لا) negative in both places; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); (إلى أهله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ذهب).
The clause «لا صدّق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا صلّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كذّب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كذّب.
The clause «ذهب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كذّب or تولّى.
The clause «يتمطّى ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of ذهب.

* Morphology:
(صلّى): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, and its origin is a wāw, because the plural of الصلاة is صلوات.. the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif; its pattern is فعّل.
(يتمطّى): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, and its origin is a wāw, for it is taken from المطا, which is the back; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif; its pattern is يتفعّل.

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أولى) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being العقاب "the punishment" or الهلاك "destruction" [Note: Al-Maḥallī reported that (أولى) is a verbal noun with the sense of a past verb (ism fiʿl māḍin), meaning "evil after evil has come close to you", and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to what is understood from the context, i.e. evil or what you dislike; the lām in (لك) is for clarification (al-tabyīn), so it is redundant, and the second-person pronoun is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the second أولى is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. the content of the meaning of the first أولى.]; (لك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أولى); (الفاء) conjunction; the second (أولى) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. the threat or the evil; (ثمّ) a conjunction..
The clause «(العقاب) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(هو) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أولى لك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause, for emphasis.
The clause «(هو) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أولى لك.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of reproach; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative; (سدى) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun of يترك.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يترك) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسب.
The clause «يحسب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يترك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(سدى): a derived adjective for singular and plural; one says إبل سدى, i.e. neglected camels.. And (الألف) is converted from a yāʾ.. Al-ʿUkbarī said: the alif is converted from a wāw.. In al-Miṣbāḥ it comes: سديت الأرض فهي سدية, of the pattern-class تعب, "its dew became abundant"; and سدا الرجل سدوا, of the pattern-class قال, "he stretched his hand towards the thing"; and سدا البعير سدوا, "the camel stretched its foreleg in walking".. and أسديته "I left it سدى", i.e. neglected.

safi-cedvel:37-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (يك) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the sukūn appearing on the nūn that is omitted for lightening; (من منيّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (نطفة); and the pronoun is the noun of (كان), referring to المنيّ; and the fāʿil (agent) of (خلق) is a pronoun referring to Allah, and likewise (سوّى) and (جعل); (منه) attached to (جعل), by making it carry the meaning of خلق; (الذكر) badal (substitute) of الزوجين, accusative.
The clause «لم يك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يمنى ...» is in the position of a genitive: naʿt of منيّ.
The clause «كان ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم يك.
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «سوّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
40- (الهمزة) is like the first; (قادر) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ليس; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحيي..) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (قادر).
The clause «ليس ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(منيّ): a noun for the male's fluid ejected into the womb; its pattern is فعيل.
(يمنى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يمني: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(سوّى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion; its original form is سوّي — with yāʾ at its end —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(الموتى): plural of ميّت.. see verse (28) of Surat al-Baqara.

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {فَاقِرَةٌ}: it is the great calamity; it was so named because it breaks the vertebrae (faqār) of the back. al-Nābigha said:
4418 - أَبَى لِيَ قَبْرٌ لا يزالُ مُقابِليْ ... وضَرْبَةُ فَأْسٍ فوقَ رَأْسيَ فاقِرَهْ
(A grave that ever faces me, and the blow of an axe upon my head, a back-breaking one, refused me [rest].)
That is: a calamity that leaves its mark. From this the poor man (al-faqīr) was named, because his vertebrae are broken by want; this has already been discussed in al-Baqara.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {التراقي}: the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «بَلَغَتْ», and the fāʿil (agent) is an implied pronoun [referring] to the soul, even though it has not been mentioned, as in the saying of Ḥātim:
4419 - أماوِيَّ ما يُغْنِي الثَّراءُ عن الفتى ... إذا حَشْرَجَتْ يوماً وضاقَ بها الصدرُ
(O Māwiyya, wealth avails a man nothing when one day it rattles [in his throat] and the chest is straitened by it.)
That is: when the soul rattles. It has been said about the verse: what points to the soul is the mention of the whole that comprises it, namely the wealthy man; likewise here the mention of the human being points to the soul.
